cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication out-of-bounds write in MSRP message body parsing

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, msrp_parse_buffer() subtracted delimiter framing from a peer-controlled short segment whose MSRP byte range ended in * without first proving the segment was long enough. The unsigned result wrapped near SIZE_MAX and reached switch_msrp_msg_set_payload() as both an allocation size and memcpy length, while related pointer arithmetic could read before the receive buffer. The listener is disabled by default in msrp.conf.xml, but any deployment enabling an MSRP TCP or TLS port parses this framing before authentication. An unauthenticated network peer can corrupt memory and crash FreeSWITCH, dropping all active calls, although remote code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

cna.title: FileBrowser Quantum: Symlink following escapes user scope allowing arbitrary file read outside the served directory

descriptions.value: FileBrowser Quantum is a free, self-hosted, web-based file manager. Prior to 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta, file read handling in backend/pkg/indexing/indexingFiles.go resolves symbolic links through GetRealPath without confirming that the resolved target remains inside the source root and the user's authorized scope. Download, preview, media, OnlyOffice, and public-share read flows that enable FollowSymlinks can therefore serve an out-of-scope target through a reachable in-scope symlink. An authenticated user with download access can read server-accessible files outside the assigned scope, and a holder of a public share link can do the same without an account when the shared directory exposes such a symlink. This issue is fixed in 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta.

An authenticated room member who establishes a WebRTC connection can send mouse and keyboard events through the legacy control channel while controls are locked or the member is otherwise unauthorized by the modern control API. cna.title: undici vulnerable to cross-user information disclosure via cross-origin redirect revalidation

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, when an Agent composes the redirect and shared cache interceptors, a cached response that is revalidated with a conditional request can be validated by a 304 Not Modified from a different origin. When the origin that stored the response redirects the conditional revalidation request to another origin, the redirect handler strips origin-bound credential headers but not the cache-generated If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since validators, so the redirect destination receives the original origin's validator and undici treats its 304 as successful revalidation of the stored representation. As a result, a shared cache can serve the original origin's stored authenticated response, including one gated by Authorization, to a later unauthenticated caller. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, compose the interceptors as cache then redirect, use per-origin dispatchers and cache stores, or disable shared caching on redirect-capable requests.

cna.title: Seroval: Script injection through RegExp sources in serialized output

descriptions.value: Seroval facilitates JavaScript value stringification, including complex structures beyond JSON.stringify capabilities. Prior to 1.0.0 and from 1.5.5 until 1.6.10, the JavaScript-output APIs serialize a RegExp source containing a less-than character without the escaping needed for an HTML script element. An application is affected when it builds regular expression syntax from untrusted input, serializes that RegExp through serialize, serializeAsync, crossSerialize, crossSerializeAsync, crossSerializeStream, Serializer, or compileJSON, and embeds the result in an HTML script element. The crafted source can terminate the element and execute script in the page received by another user. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.10.

cna.title: pgAdmin 4: libpq uses the pgAdmin service account's own password file and client certificate

scenarios.value: Any authenticated user who can register a server. Attack Complexity is High: the service account must have a password file entry or client certificate that a server the attacker can reach accepts, a deployment condition the attacker does not control. Scope is Changed because the connection is made with the service account's database credentials, an identity the attacker was never granted; Confidentiality and Integrity are High on that database server. Availability is None.

Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry. AT:P for the service account's credential and an accepting server. VC:H because the service account's stored secret is used through pgAdmin; SC:H/SI:H for the database server reached with that identity.

descriptions.value:
When a server in pgAdmin 4 had no password file, client certificate or client key configured, or the configured one could not be found, pgAdmin left the parameter out of the connection and libpq fell back to the defaults of the operating-system account running pgAdmin: ~/.pgpass, ~/.postgresql/postgresql.crt and postgresql.key, or PGPASSFILE, PGSSLCERT and PGSSLKEY. In server mode any user could therefore connect to a server with the service account's saved passwords or client certificate, and supplying only a copy of its public certificate was enough for libpq to pair it with the service account's private key. A pg_service.conf entry, or a maintenance database name read as a connection string by pg_dumpall, could bring the same files back for the utilities.

The fix gives each of these parameters a value in server mode, the user's own file or otherwise a path that can never be opened, in the connection string, in the environment of the utilities and in the --dbname connection string that ranks above a service entry. Desktop mode is unchanged.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication invalid pointer dereference in mod_rtmp connect command handling

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, rtmp_i_connect() passed the first RTMP connect argument to amf0_object_get() without checking whether the AMF value was an object. A string or number in place of an AMF object caused union bytes from the message to be interpreted as node pointers and dereferenced. Any client with network access to an enabled mod_rtmp listener could send the malformed connect command before login; the module is disabled in the stock build and configuration. The invalid read reliably crashes FreeSWITCH and ends every active call, while no write, memory disclosure, or code execution has been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

descriptions.description: CWE-843: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication heap out-of-bounds write in mod_xml_rpc WebSocket frame length handling

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, ws_read_frame() decoded a WebSocket frame's 64-bit extended payload length with a 32-bit byte swap and narrowed the result into a signed length. A value whose surviving low word became negative bypassed the signed size check and was reinterpreted as an enormous unsigned count, causing client bytes to overwrite memory beyond the 64 KiB receive buffer. Any client completing a /socket WebSocket upgrade on an enabled mod_xml_rpc endpoint reached the parser before HTTP authentication; both the module and WebSocket endpoint are disabled by default. The heap overwrite can corrupt connection pointers and crash FreeSWITCH, ending every concurrent session, although remote code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

cna.title: LimeSurvey Community Edition 7.8.0 - SQL injection via Archive Attributes

descriptions.value: CAPEC-66 SQL Injection

solutions.value: Apply an upstream patch that strictly validates imported participant attribute identifiers and always quotes schema-derived identifiers before constructing the SPSS export SELECT list. Upgrade to the vendor-fixed release once one is published.

supportingMedia.value: Apply an upstream patch that strictly validates imported participant attribute identifiers and always quotes schema-derived identifiers before constructing the SPSS export SELECT list. Upgrade to the vendor-fixed release once one is published.

workarounds.value: Do not grant untrusted accounts global survey-creation permission and do not import untrusted .lsa archives. Review imported participant-table schemas for unexpected attribute column names.

supportingMedia.value: Do not grant untrusted accounts global survey-creation permission and do not import untrusted .lsa archives. Review imported participant-table schemas for unexpected attribute column names.

descriptions.value: LimeSurvey Community Edition 7.8.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the survey-archive participant import and SPSS-response export workflow. An authenticated user with global surveys.create permission can import a crafted .lsa archive whose participant XML creates an attacker-named attribute column. When the user exports responses from the imported non-anonymous survey, LimeSurvey passes the persisted name to Yii's select builder. Names containing parentheses are treated as SQL expressions instead of quoted identifiers, causing attacker-controlled SQL to execute with the application's database privileges.

supportingMedia.value: LimeSurvey Community Edition 7.8.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the survey-archive participant import and SPSS-response export workflow. An authenticated user with global surveys.create permission can import a crafted .lsa archive whose participant XML creates an attacker-named attribute column. cna.title: pgAdmin 4: SSH tunnels use the pgAdmin service account's own SSH identity

scenarios.value: Any authenticated user who can register a server with an SSH tunnel. Attack Complexity is High: the service account must have an unencrypted default key, agent or configuration that a host the attacker can name accepts. Scope is Changed because the tunnel authenticates as the service account to another system, an identity the attacker was never granted; Confidentiality and Integrity are High for the access it gives. Availability is None.

Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry. AT:P for the service account's SSH identity and an accepting host. VC:H because the service account's key is used through pgAdmin; SC:H/SI:H for the SSH host and the network reached through it.

descriptions.value:
pgAdmin 4 opens SSH tunnels with the sshtunnel library but gave it neither host_pkey_directories nor ssh_config_file, so it always loaded the unencrypted private keys in ~/.ssh of the operating-system account running pgAdmin, read that account's ~/.ssh/config (IdentityFile, User, HostName, ProxyCommand) for the tunnel host, and could use its ssh-agent. In server mode any user could therefore configure a tunnel to a host that accepts the service account's key, with no credentials of their own or with an identity file that did not exist in their storage, and reach it as that account.

The fix makes tunnels in server mode use only the identity file or password the user configured: the service account's keys, configuration and agent are no longer used, and an identity file that cannot be found in the user's storage is reported instead of falling back to ~/.ssh. Desktop mode is unchanged.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Body 1.23_01 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl leave the temporary file of an incomplete multipart upload on disk.

The multipart parser creates a temporary file as soon as a file part starts, but adds it to the upload list only when the part completes. Uploads are only ever deleted from that list, by the cleanup option or by the caller, so a body that ends inside a file part leaves its temporary file where nothing can find it.

A remote attacker can fill the temporary directory by repeating such requests, leaving one file behind for each.

cna.title: pgAdmin 4: Import/Export Data query export runs a command through a backslash in a double-quoted identifier

scenarios.value: Same threat model and outcome as CVE-2026-17566, of which this is a bypass: any authenticated user with the Import/Export Data permission (granted by default) and an ordinary database role, which can set standard_conforming_strings itself, so Attack Complexity is Low. Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability are High for command execution on the pgAdmin host. Scope is Changed, as for CVE-2026-17566, because the command runs on the pgAdmin host rather than within the database server the user is connected to.

Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry and the same vector as CVE-2026-17566. AT:N because no condition outside the attacker's control is needed. VC/VI/VA:H for the pgAdmin host and SC/SI/SA:H for the systems reachable from it with its credentials.

descriptions.value:
pgAdmin 4's Import/Export Data tool wraps a user's query export in a psql \copy (...) TO command and checks that the query's parentheses are balanced so that nothing can escape the wrapper. The check rejected a backslash inside a single-quoted string, but not inside a double-quoted identifier, where it treated the next double quote as closing the identifier. psql's \copy parser applies the connection's escape character to whichever quote opened a token, so with standard_conforming_strings off a backslash-escaped double quote does not close the identifier. pgAdmin's and psql's view of the quoting then diverged, a closing parenthesis hidden from the check ended the \copy (...) wrapper, and a following TO PROGRAM clause was executed by psql on the pgAdmin host, as the operating-system account running pgAdmin, before the server rejected the statement. An ordinary database role can turn standard_conforming_strings off for itself, and the Import/Export Data permission is granted to non-administrators by default.

This is a bypass of the fix for CVE-2026-17566. The fix rejects any backslash inside a double-quoted identifier, as was already done for single-quoted strings, since its meaning depends on a server setting that cannot be known reliably when the query is validated.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Body 1.23_01 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via an unbounded multipart part header block.

The multipart parser takes everything up to the first blank line after a boundary as the part's header block, with no limit on its size or number of lines. Every line is stored in the part's header hash, so a block of short lines costs about 60 bytes of memory per input byte.

A remote attacker can exhaust worker memory with a single request.

Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry. AT:P for the timing and configuration conditions, UI:P because the victim only has to use the PSQL tool. VC:H for the leaked password; SC:H/SI:L for the database server it opens.

descriptions.value:
To pass a server's password to psql and to the utilities pgAdmin 4 runs as background processes, the server manager wrote it into pgAdmin's own process environment: as PGPASSWORD for the PSQL tool, and under a per-process variable for a utility. Nothing removed it afterwards. pgAdmin's environment is shared by every user's requests and copied into every process it starts, so in server mode another user's later PSQL session or utility inherited the password, and libpq used PGPASSWORD for any connection made without a password of its own, letting one user connect with another user's saved password.

The fix puts the password only into the environment built for the process that needs it and starts psql with a copy of pgAdmin's environment instead of the environment itself.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

solutions.value: Upgrade to MIME-tools 5.521 or later.

descriptions.value:
MIME::Parser versions before 5.521 for Perl set no limit on the number of message parts by default, allowing memory exhaustion.

The max_parts option defaulted to -1, which disables the limit, so a parser created with default settings builds an entity for every part however many a message has.

Version 5.521 sets max_parts to 1000 and max_depth to 64 by default. Setting either to -1 still removes the limit.

cna.title: RE2JS: Quadratic-time denial of service in re2js lookbehind matching

descriptions.value: RE2JS is the JavaScript port of RE2, a regular expression engine that provides linear time matching. From 2.2.0 until 2.8.7, enabling LOOKBEHINDS and using repeated matching through matcher().find(), matchAll(), split(), or matcher().replaceAll() can cause quadratic total work. Machine.match restarts lookbehind scanning from offset zero for each requested start position, while Matcher-based APIs request capture slots that prevent the early exit used for captureless matching. Dense matches therefore repeatedly rescan the input, allowing attacker-influenced text to monopolize a single-threaded worker and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.7.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication stack buffer overflow in mod_rtmp control-message handling

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, rtmp_handle_control() rendered an RTMP user-control message into a 200-byte stack buffer using an unbounded sprintf loop controlled by the wire message length. A body of roughly 70 bytes or more overflowed the stack before any RTMP login, because the handshake authenticates neither side. The flaw affects deployments that build and load mod_rtmp, which is disabled in the stock build and configuration but commonly exposes a listener on TCP port 1935 when enabled. One unauthenticated message can crash FreeSWITCH and end every active call; the constrained ASCII hex output has not yielded control-flow hijacking. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

descriptions.value:
Description:

When an iRule that processes client traffic using the GENERICMESSAGE::route command is configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE).

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication process termination in the Event Socket via an unbounded Content-Length

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, mod_event_socket used an unauthenticated Content-Length value directly as the allocation size for an Event Socket message body. Negative or extremely large values could overflow the terminator calculation or force an allocation failure through a helper that aborts the FreeSWITCH process. The header is parsed before the Event Socket password, so any host admitted by apply-inbound-acl can trigger termination with its first packet; the default loopback ACL limits ordinary installations to local clients. The outbound socket dialplan path is also affected when FreeSWITCH connects to a hostile application server, and process termination drops every active call until the service is restarted. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

cna.title: Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl send a body in responses to HEAD requests, corrupting the next response on a persistent or pipelined connection

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starlet 0.33 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl send a body in responses to HEAD requests, corrupting the next response on a persistent or pipelined connection.

The request method is not passed to the response writer, so whatever body the application returns for a HEAD request is sent. With Plack::Middleware::Head the body is empty, but an HTTP/1.1 response without a Content-Length header still gets the chunked encoding terminator. Responses with status 204 or 304 are also sent with their body.

Pipelined GET and HEAD requests keep the connection open even when keep-alive is disabled, which is the default. A client or proxy reading the connection takes the extra bytes as the start of the next response, which may desynchronize a proxy that shares the connection across clients.

cna.title: pgAdmin 4: Utility binary path can point at a shared storage directory

scenarios.value: Any authenticated user who can upload to a shared storage directory and set their binary path. Attack Complexity is High: SHARED_STORAGE must be configured and writable by the user, and the platform must let an uploaded file run (Windows server mode; on POSIX uploads are not executable). Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability are High for code execution as the pgAdmin service account. Scope is Unchanged, following CVE-2026-17347: the code runs with the authority pgAdmin already holds.
Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry. AT:P for the deployment and platform conditions. VC:H/VI:H/VA:H for code execution as the pgAdmin account; no subsequent-system impact is claimed.

descriptions.value:
pgAdmin 4 runs pg_dump, pg_restore, pg_dumpall and psql from the binary path a user sets in their preferences. In server mode the binary path was refused only when it lay under the per-user storage directory (STORAGE_DIR), not under a SHARED_STORAGE directory, which ordinary users can upload files to. A user could therefore upload an executable to shared storage, point their binary path at it, and have pgAdmin run it as the operating-system account running pgAdmin. On POSIX, files created through pgAdmin are not executable, so this is exploitable where any file with an executable name can run, such as Windows server mode.

The fix checks the binary path against every SHARED_STORAGE directory as well, after expanding $DIR, collapsing ".." and resolving symbolic links, compares directories in a way a different spelling on a case-insensitive filesystem cannot bypass, refuses a path containing a NUL, and enforces the check wherever binary paths are resolved, including for the PSQL tool.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Body 1.23_01 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl allow memory and temporary file exhaustion via an unlimited number of form fields and multipart parts.

The urlencoded parser splits the whole body on its separators at once, creating one scalar per separator before any field is stored. This costs about 90 bytes of memory per separator byte. The multipart parser creates a temporary file for every part that carries a filename. Neither parser limits how many fields or parts a body may hold.

A remote attacker can exhaust worker memory with a body made of separators, or create thousands of temporary files with one request of small file parts.

cna.title: russh's SSH client is susceptible to unbounded allocations via EXT_INFO packets

descriptions.value: russh is a Rust SSH client and server library that includes an SSH agent protocol implementation. Prior to 0.65.0, the client Session::process_packet path in russh/src/client/encrypted.rs accepts repeated packets encoded with russh's private msg::EXT_INFO = 7 before authentication, while the standards-compliant EXT_INFO message number 82 does not reach the affected handler. The handle_ext_info function appends every parsed extension name to received_extensions without clearing, deduplicating, or bounding the vector. A malicious SSH server that deliberately sends private message number 7 can therefore retain an unbounded number of attacker-controlled extension names for the session lifetime, causing progressive client memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in version 0.65.0.

cna.title: MIME::Field::ParamVal versions before 5.521 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unclosed comments in header parameters

solutions.value: Upgrade to MIME-tools 5.521 or later.

descriptions.value:
MIME::Field::ParamVal versions before 5.521 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unclosed comments in header parameters.

The comment pattern used to parse Content-Type and Content-Disposition parameters scans from each "(" to the next ")". In a field with no ")", every "(" scans to the end of the header and fails, so parsing takes time quadratic in the header length. The field is parsed again on each attribute lookup, several times per MIME entity.

A 40 KB header takes about 7 seconds to parse once.

cna.title: Vaultwarden: Icon endpoint SSRF fix bypass via second-stage favicon IP literal URLs

descriptions.value: Vaultwarden is a Bitwarden-compatible server written in Rust. Prior to version 1.37.0, the Vaultwarden icon downloader validates the initial icon host and DNS results but passes favicon URLs parsed from attacker-controlled HTML to get_page_with_referer() without applying should_block_host() to the second-stage host. This flaw bypasses the remediation for CVE-2026-47160, which covered decimal, hexadecimal, octal, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 host normalization, because the second-stage IP-literal favicon fetch does not invoke the custom DNS resolver. A remote unauthenticated attacker can provide a public page whose favicon uses an IP-literal URL, allowing the Vaultwarden server to reach loopback or private and internal addresses. The issue affects instances with internal icon downloading enabled and can expose internal responses that resemble supported images or reveal reachability through timing, status, and cache behavior. This issue is fixed in version 1.37.0.

cna.title: Gssproxy: gssproxy: null pointer dereference in gssx_init_sec_context crashes daemon

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Andrey Vasilevsky for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
There is no way to fully mitigate this vulnerability without applying a code fix. The gssproxy Unix socket must be world-accessible for normal operation, and the default configuration accepts connections from any local user.

As a partial workaround, administrators can add "Restart=on-failure" to the gssproxy systemd unit to enable automatic restarts after a crash. This does not prevent the crash but limits the denial-of-service window. Note that a persistent attacker can still outpace the restart cycle.

descriptions.value: A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability was found in gssproxy. When a GSSX_INIT_SEC_CONTEXT request is received with the target_name field absent, the daemon dereferences the resulting NULL pointer and crashes. The request requires no authentication, allowing any local user to crash the gssproxy daemon via its Unix socket. The daemon does not automatically restart, resulting in a persistent denial of service that also affects dependent services such as Kerberized NFS and IdM.

cna.title: compress zstd: Panic on two-block frames

descriptions.value: compress provides various compression algorithms. Prior to 1.20.2, the zstd DecodeAll and streaming decoder paths can panic when a crafted two-block frame reaches huff0.ReadTable with an FSE normalized count of 32768 that readNCount stores in int16 as -32768. The wrapped count allows buildDtable to retain stale fse.Scratch decode-table state from the prior block, and nextFast then derives an out-of-range state and indexes beyond the table instead of returning a decode error. Both blocks are required to preserve and then reuse the stale state, allowing untrusted zstd input to crash an application. This issue is fixed in version 1.20.2.

descriptions.value: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instruction only after the entire literal had been received. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send an insert instruction on the QPACK encoder stream that declares an arbitrarily large literal and then keep sending data, causing the decoder to buffer it without bound for the lifetime of the connection and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service. The issue occurs regardless of the advertised QPACK dynamic table capacity, including when the dynamic table is disabled. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

cna.title: Zuke: Command-form registry descriptors bypass the MCP launch policy

descriptions.value: Zuke is a code-first, strongly typed build automation system for Deno. Prior to 1.51.0, the @zuke/core MCP registry mode accepts command-form registry descriptors without applying the ZUKE_REGISTRY_LAUNCH_HOSTS authorization enforced for remote module descriptors. When zuke mcp --registry --allow-run reads a registry writable by another party and a run-capable caller invokes the affected tool, the registry writer can choose the program and arguments executed with the operator's environment and workspace access. The --allow-run and --protect name globs do not contain the issue because the descriptor supplies those names, and the optional destructive confirmation displays a description controlled by the same writer. The local default registry populated only through zuke register is not affected because that command writes module-form descriptors. This issue is fixed in version 1.51.0.

cna.title: frr: ospf6d fails to enforce all OSPFv3 packets use IPv6 link-local addresses

credits.value: Bing Shui <bingshui@smail.nju.edu.cn> (not reported as security issue)

workarounds.value:
Either:

  *  configure OSPFv3 authentication trailers ("ipv6 ospf6 authentication")
  *  or ensure through firewall configuration that only packets with link-local or multicast destination addresses are accepted on input for IPv6 protocol 89 (OSPF). Note that checking the source address is insufficient, as some routers may (unexpectedly) forward packets with global-scoped IPv6 destination addresses even if they have link-local source addresses.

descriptions.value:
In all prior released versions of FRRouting, the OSPFv3 (for IPv6) implementation does not check that OSPFv3 packets have a link-local source address and either a link-local destination or one of the protocol multicast destination groups.  This may enable malicious actors to establish OSPFv3 adjacencies from unexpectedly, distant IPv6 hosts. Proper usage of OSPFv3 authentication trailers (RFC 7166, as is best practice) prevents full exploitation of this issue, though may allow a malicious actor to waste CPU on authentication checks.


Note the linked PR #23935 is not sufficient to fix the issue as it only verifies the source address. It is the destination address that must be checked.


Required configuration: The OSPFv3 for IPv6 routing protocol must be running (ospf6d process) and in use (enabled globally with "router ospf6" and on specific interfaces with "ipv6 ospf6 area".)


Workaround: either:

  *  configure OSPFv3 authentication trailers ("ipv6 ospf6 authentication")
  *  or ensure through firewall configuration that only packets with link-local or multicast destination addresses are accepted on input for IPv6 protocol 89 (OSPF). Note that checking the source address is insufficient, as some routers may (unexpectedly) forward packets with global-scoped IPv6 destination addresses even if they have link-local source addresses.

descriptions.description: CWE-304 Missing critical step in authentication: protocol interactions should be limited to IPv6 link-local scope

This issue is fixed in version 4.6.3.

cna.title: MariaDB Connector/J: Server could switch character_set_results away from UTF-8 without the client noticing

descriptions.value: MariaDB Connector/J is used to connect applications developed in Java to MariaDB and MySQL databases. cna.title: pyasn1: Quadratic CPU consumption in constructed BIT STRING decoding

descriptions.value: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. Prior to 0.6.5, constructed BIT STRING decoding repeatedly shifts and copies the complete bit value accumulated from earlier fragments. Attacker-controlled BER or CER input contains many constructed BIT STRING fragments; schema-driven DER also accepts a definite-length constructed BIT STRING. BitStringPayloadDecoder repeatedly calls BitString.fromOctetString with the prior bitString as prepend, shifting an ever-growing SizedInteger for each fragment and causing quadratic work. Large fragmented values can exhaust CPU during decode() without requiring later conversion or formatting. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

The caller's user id is used only to annotate the response, allowing any authenticated user who obtains another collection's id to read the owner's identity, collection name and description, reviews, and complete item list across the tenant boundary. A malicious or compromised server, or a machine-in-the-middle attacker, could declare a very large length or send an empty response before any password was transmitted. cna.title: pyasn1: Quadratic CPU use in schemaless BER/CER/DER container decoding

descriptions.value: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. From 0.3.3 until 0.6.5, schemaless container decoding stores every decoded component's TagSet in a growing set even though only one-versus-multiple tag types must be distinguished. Attacker-controlled BER, CER, or DER input contains many distinct long tag IDs whose TagSet hashes collide. Each later set insertion compares against an increasing number of earlier colliding tags in ConstructedPayloadDecoderBase._decodeComponentsSchemaless, producing quadratic CPU work while decoded values and order remain valid. Repeated inputs can exhaust decoder CPU and reduce service availability. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

cna.title: PipesHub before 0.10.0 SSRF via Image URLs in Indexed Documents

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: PipesHub before 0.10.0 SSRF via Image URLs in Indexed Documents

cna.title: joserfc: Unbounded JWE General JSON `recipients` Array Leads to CPU Exhaustion (DoS) via Repeated RSA Private-Key Decryption

descriptions.value: joserfc is a Python library that provides an implementation of several JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) standards. Prior to 1.7.5, joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json() accepts a JWE General JSON Serialization recipients array without a count limit and calls decrypt_cek() for every entry. An unauthenticated attacker who can submit a JWE to an endpoint using an RSA key-management algorithm can choose the number of private-key decryption operations performed by one request. The verify_all_recipients option does not reduce this work because the affected loop processes every recipient before consulting that setting, allowing repeated requests to exhaust service CPU without affecting confidentiality or integrity. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.5.

cna.title: Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash <= 3.8.2 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via 'email' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions up to, and including, 3.8.2 via the `email` parameter of the `uo_login_action()` function. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in which the plugin's account-verification gate resolves the submitted `email` value using the raw, unsanitized string passed to `get_user_by()`, while the subsequent `wp_signon()` call relies on WordPress core's internal `sanitize_user()` to strip appended junk characters — causing the gate lookup to fail and be skipped entirely while the real account is still resolved and authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in to unverified or administrator-suspended accounts whose credentials they already possess, obtaining a valid `wordpress_logged_in` session cookie and defeating the plugin's account-approval and account-suspension controls. The nonce required to reach the handler is freely obtainable in the same request from the unauthenticated `ult-refresh-nonce` endpoint, making exploitation trivial for any attacker with network access to the site and knowledge of a target account's credentials.

cna.title: Forge: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery via non-canonical DigestInfo encoding

descriptions.value: Forge, also called node-forge, is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, publicKey.verify() with the default RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5 scheme in lib/rsa.js parses the recovered DigestInfo with the lenient BER parser asn1.fromDer() and validates its structure with digestInfoValidator without requiring canonical DER bytes. Non-minimal or indefinite lengths, malformed parameter values, and non-canonical object identifier encodings with padded subidentifiers or trailing bytes can leave attacker-controlled data inside an accepted DigestInfo. When the verifying RSA public key uses a low exponent such as e=3, an attacker can use that encoding slack to forge a signature without the private key. The same path is used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 signature verification. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

descriptions.description: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

descriptions.value: Tesseract is an open source OCR engine. Prior to 5.5.4, ReadAdaptedClass in src/classify/adaptive.cpp raw-reads an ADAPT_CLASS_STRUCT from a pre-adapted-template .a file without neutralizing TempProtos and Config pointer fields before any destructor path. When the legacy engine is selected, classify_use_pre_adapted_templates is enabled, and an attacker can write the output-basename .a file, the success or rejection path can pass file-controlled pointers to ~ADAPT_CLASS_STRUCT and operator delete, causing memory corruption and denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 5.5.4.

cna.title: UsersWP <= 1.2.78 - Unauthenticated Account Access via Predictable Dummy User Password Disclosed through Registration Form Hash

affected.product: UsersWP – Front-end login form, User Registration, User Profile & Members Directory plugin for WP

descriptions.value: The UsersWP – Front-end login form, User Registration, User Profile & Members Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized account access via Use of Predictable Password in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.78 The vulnerability exists because `get_dummy_user_passowrd()` derives the shared password for all 25 built-in dummy user accounts as the first 15 characters of `substr(hash('SHA256', AUTH_KEY . site_url()), 0, 25)`, while the full 25-character value of that same hash is simultaneously embedded in the hidden `uwp_register_hash` field rendered on every registration form response — reachable without authentication via both the public `/register/` page and the `wp_ajax_nopriv_uwp_ajax_register_form` AJAX handler, even when user registration is disabled. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover the dummy user password directly from a single HTTP request and use it to authenticate as any of the 25 built-in dummy accounts (such as antawn, chynna, or kiki) through `wp-login.php`, potentially achieving privilege escalation if any dummy account holds an elevated role. Exploitation requires that an administrator has previously created dummy users via the plugin's Tools page.

cna.title: Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by flattening legacy webhook payloads before checking their signature

solutions.value: Upgrade to Business-GoCardless 1.01 or later.

descriptions.value:
Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by flattening legacy webhook payloads before checking their signature.

A webhook body with a top-level "payload" key is verified as a legacy webhook. To rebuild the signed string, the payload is flattened into one key and value pair per leaf, each key carrying the full path to that leaf, and the pairs are then encoded, sorted and joined. A long key holding a long array costs memory proportional to the key length times the array length.

A remote attacker can exhaust memory in the process receiving webhooks with a single request that carries no valid signature.

cna.title: Next.js: Cross-client response injection and disclosure in self-hosted Next.js applications forwarding fetched responses

descriptions.value: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. Prior to 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js App Router route handlers and the fetch cache that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. When the application is behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that permits pipelined response queueing, a crafted upstream response can desynchronize responses between clients. The resulting desynchronization can inject a response into another client's queue or disclose another client's response. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

cna.title: croc: Overwrite-confirmation bypass via a crafted "croc-stdin-" filename on receive

descriptions.description: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

descriptions.value: croc is a tool that allows any two computers to simply and securely transfer files and folders. Prior to 11.5.2, the receive-side file-readiness loop in src/croc/croc.go treats any sender-controlled basename beginning with croc-stdin- as a trusted text-transfer artifact even when SendingText is false. This skips askReceiveOverwrite and rename handling for a predictable exact-name collision in the receiver's working directory, allowing a remote sender whose transfer the user accepts to overwrite or truncate a matching regular file through recipientInitializeFile, or to remove and replace a matching destination with an empty file or an in-directory symlink through createEmptyFileAndFinish, without confirmation. The impact is limited to pre-existing names in the croc-stdin- namespace that the sender can predict; other filenames retain the prompt, dotfiles outside that namespace are not reachable, and symlink targets remain confined to the receive directory. This issue is fixed in version 11.5.2.

cna.title: Next.js: Information disclosure across root params when a 'use cache' function is called through unstable_cache()

descriptions.value: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.3.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications using the same 'use cache' function directly during rendering and through unstable_cache() can disclose cached data across root params when that function reads a root param. During the first fill after a cold process start, cross-request deduplication allows a concurrent unstable_cache() request to join the direct call's in-flight fill and receive its result before the root param mismatch is rejected. unstable_cache() then persists that result under a key that omits root params, causing later requests for other root param values to receive the same entry until revalidation or eviction. Exploitation requires the unstable_cache() request to arrive while the first fill is in flight. Outside this race, nesting 'use cache' inside unstable_cache() raises an unsupported-operation error, and avoiding that nesting prevents the issue. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

cna.title: Next.js: Cache leak across root param values in nested 'use cache' functions via delayed inner stream metadata

descriptions.value: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.2.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications with Cache Components enabled can reuse an outer 'use cache' entry across root param values when a nested 'use cache' call reads a root param through next/root-params and returns a value containing pending promises. React Flight can deliver the ready portion to the outer function before the inner cache finishes publishing its root-param dependencies. The outer entry can then complete and be persisted under a key that omits the root param, causing the first written value to be served for other root param values and allowing the outer entry to ignore nested cache tag invalidation and lifetimes. The leaked value is not attacker controlled and depends on which invocation writes the entry first. This variant does not require an existing inner cache entry or a slow cache handler and is not covered by the fix for CVE-2026-103004. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

descriptions.value: The Advanced Product Fields (Product Addons) for WooCommerce WordPress plugin from 1.6.22 to 1.7.3 does not validate that a submitted value for a required paid product option matches one of the configured choices, only that it is not empty, allowing unauthenticated users to add a product to the cart and complete an order while skipping the required option's surcharge and paying only the base product price.

cna.title: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-34 Heap Buffer Overflow via -morph Option

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-34 Heap Buffer Overflow via -morph Option

descriptions.value: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-34 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in its -morph processing, where crafted images cause writes beyond the bounds of a heap buffer. An attacker can supply a crafted image that, when processed by a user with the -morph option, corrupts heap memory and crashes the application.

cna.title: Windows USB Audio Class driver (usbaudio.sys) Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

references.name: Windows USB Audio Class driver (usbaudio.sys) Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

descriptions.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows USB Audio Class driver (usbaudio.sys) allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.

cna.title: GluonTS arbitrary file write during archive extraction

descriptions.value: CAPEC-132 Symlink Attack

Path traversal in the archive extraction utility in GluonTS before 0.17.0 might allow an actor who supplies a crafted tar archive to write arbitrary files outside the intended extraction directory with the privileges of the extracting process via symbolic or hard links contained in the archive.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.17.0 or later.

cna.title: Forge: Denial of service in TLS record processing via a record interleaved with a fragmented handshake message

descriptions.value: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, the affected implementation used forge.tls.createConnection(), fragmented handshake message, interleaved record to process the relevant input or security decision. node-forge continued processing after a TLS record of another content type interrupted a fragmented handshake message. A remote peer could trigger an uncaught TypeError in process(), causing the connection or hosting process to fail. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

cna.title: WPBakery Page Builder <= 9.0.1 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Post Author Display Name

descriptions.value: The WPBakery Page Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'display_name / nickname' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.0.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution requires that at least one public post attributed to the attacker's account be rendered through a Basic Grid using a Grid Builder template with the Post Author element configured to link to the post author; Author-level users can satisfy this precondition unassisted, while Subscribers depend on an administrator having assigned or published a post under their account.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Lago through 1.55.0 Cross-Organization Invoice Payment Manipulation via Stripe Webhook

descriptions.value: Lago through 1.55.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Invoices::Payments::StripeService that allows users of one organization to mark another organization's invoice as paid due to an unscoped invoice lookup. Attackers controlling their organization's Stripe integration can sign a payment_intent.succeeded event carrying a victim invoice UUID to unlock wallet top-ups or payment-gated subscriptions.

Teachers with question import or lesson edit rights can upload a crafted zip with img src values containing ../ sequences, copying server files like config.php into their draft area.

Attackers can pass crafted values through applications forwarding user input into the OVER clause to execute SQL with the database connection's privileges.

cna.title: Munshi Payment Bypass via Unauthenticated Webhook Endpoint

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Munshi Payment Bypass via Unauthenticated Webhook Endpoint

descriptions.value: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-06-30 contained a payment bypass vulnerability in its subscription payment webhook at POST /api/payment/order/webhook, which lacks webhook authentication, cryptographic signature verification, source validation, and independent server-side confirmation with the payment provider. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can submit a forged payment-success notification referencing an order obtained from the payment-status redirect URL, causing the backend to mark the subscription as paid/active and granting paid access without an actual successful payment.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in GStreamer. An integer overflow vulnerability in the AV1 LEB128 variable-length integer parser allows a remote attacker to cause a crash in applications that process AV1 media content. references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Nexbox A95X Amlogic S905X UART Unauthenticated Console Access

descriptions.value: Nexbox A95X TV boxes built on the Amlogic S905X platform contain an unauthenticated console exposed via an internal UART header on the PCB that allows physical attackers to obtain an interactive shell as uid 2000 (system) without any credentials. Attackers with physical access and a USB-to-TTL adapter can leverage this shell to reach the pppoe_wrapper vendor daemon, which contains an OS command injection vulnerability executed as root, resulting in full root-level compromise of the device.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Hyperswitch before 1.128.0 Webhook Authentication Bypass via Worldpayxml Connector

descriptions.value: Juspay Hyperswitch before 1.128.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge payment status updates because the Worldpayxml connector's verify_webhook_source always returns true without enforced mTLS. Attackers knowing the merchant_id and Worldpay orderCode can POST unsigned XML with lastEvent SETTLED to the worldpayxml webhook endpoint, marking unpaid payments as charged or triggering refund, dispute and payout events.

cna.title: pypdf: Possible infinite loop when cloning dictionaries

descriptions.value: pypdf is a free and open-source pure-python PDF library. Prior to 6.21.4, pypdf can enter an infinite loop when cloning or duplicating a crafted cyclic DictionaryObject. Clone traversal checked generated destination references rather than the original source references, allowing some source cycles to evade the visited-object check. This issue is fixed in version 6.21.4.

descriptions.description: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Bastille through 1.4.4 Jail Escape via Symlink Following in cp, rcp, jcp

descriptions.value: Bastille through 1.4.4 contains a symlink following vulnerability in the cp.sh, rcp.sh and jcp.sh subcommands that allows jailed users to escape jail isolation. Attackers inside a jail can plant symlinks pointing to host paths or other jail roots, so administrator-run copies overwrite or read host files with root privileges.

descriptions.description: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

cna.title: Welcart e-Commerce <= 2.12.5 - Account Takeover via Insecure Direct Object Reference to Unauthenticated User Input via 'member[ID]' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Welcart e-Commerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 2.12.5 via the 'member[ID]' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite any existing Welcart shop-member account's email address and password by supplying that member's numeric ID, then authenticate as that member to achieve full account takeover. The only authentication barrier is a wp_verify_nonce() check against a nonce printed to every unauthenticated visitor on the auto-published New Enrollment Form, meaning no existing account, no WordPress login, and no non-default configuration is required to exploit this vulnerability.

cna.title: Cocos Intra-handshake attested TLS implementation is vulnerable to Diversion Attacks

descriptions.value: Cocos AI is a confidential computing system for AI. In version 0.8.2 and earlier, Cocos AI accepts trusted execution environment attestation Evidence when firmware patch levels and software measurements match, without binding the Evidence to an allowed platform owner or unique machine identity and without enforcing revocation. A remote attacker who controls or compromises another platform trusted by the same verifier can substitute valid Evidence from that platform and cause authorization of the wrong platform. This vulnerability is addressed in 0.9.0. However, this vulnerability can't be patched in source code alone, since the vulnerability arises from the confidential computing threat model itself.

cna.title: Next.js: Cross-user cache disclosure and poisoning in Next.js use cache with binary arguments

descriptions.value: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.0.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js App Router applications that pass binary arguments, such as Uint8Array or Blob values, to functions using the 'use cache' directive can generate identical cache keys for distinct arguments. Requests with different binary arguments can therefore share a cached result, causing cross-user disclosure of cached data or allowing one request to poison results returned to another user. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

descriptions.description: CWE-694: Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier

cna.title: Gitea user and organization feed token scope bypass

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #40115

descriptions.value: The `/{username}` web route accepted personal access tokens over HTTP Basic authentication without checking their scope. A token confined to an unrelated scope, such as `read:issue`, could read its owner's private activity through the user RSS/Atom feed and the profile activity tab, and other members' activity in a private organization through the organization feed; a public-only token could list the owner's private repositories and organizations and render private profile READMEs. For a site administrator's token this applied to every account. Tokens are now accepted on this route only for feeds, which require `read:user` or `read:organization`.

cna.title: Forge: Denial of service in TLS record processing via call stack exhaustion

descriptions.value: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, the affected implementation used forge.tls.createConnection(), TLS record processing, process() to process the relevant input or security decision. node-forge processed received TLS records recursively, consuming one JavaScript stack frame per record in a single input chunk. A remote peer could send thousands of small records together and exhaust the call stack, causing an uncaught exception and denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Moodle through 5.3.0, 5.2.4, 5.1.8, 5.0.11 and 4.5.15 SQL Injection via enrol_database Course idnumber

descriptions.value: Moodle 5.3.0, 5.2.0 through 5.2.4, 5.1.0 through 5.1.8, 5.0.0 through 5.0.11, and through 4.5.15 contain an sql injection vulnerability in the External database enrolment plugin via course idnumber. Editing teachers can store a backslash-quote payload in idnumber that executes during scheduled sync on MySQL/MariaDB external databases, reading data and manipulating enrolment results.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

cna.title: Wekan: ReDoS via Unescaped User Input in RegExp

descriptions.value: Wekan is open source kanban built with Meteor. Prior to 11.11, the user-search publication in server/publications/users.js and the searchUsers method in server/models/users.js pass authenticated user-controlled searchTerm and query values to new RegExp() without escaping regular-expression metacharacters. MongoDB-backed deployments evaluate the resulting patterns with PCRE2, allowing a logged-in user to submit catastrophic-backtracking expressions that consume database CPU and degrade or deny service to other users; searchUsers additionally requires board membership or site-admin status. The FerretDB v1 / RE2 unaffected configuration is not practically affected by catastrophic backtracking. This issue is fixed in version 11.11.

Embedders re-entering WebAssembly via sync APIs from host functions called asynchronously can trigger runtime panics or unsound cross-thread movement of !Send host variables.

cna.title: mongofiles may disclose GridFS content to standard output through a stored filename

descriptions.value: MongoDB Database Tools mongofiles uses a database-stored GridFS filename as the output destination for get_id when --local is not specified. A user who can modify the file metadata can set the stored filename to '-', causing a later authorized retrieval to write the file contents to standard output instead of a local file. If standard output is captured in a location accessible to that user, this may disclose GridFS content the user cannot read directly. Exploitation requires a higher-privileged operator to retrieve the affected file without an explicit local destination and attacker access to the captured output. This issue affects MongoDB Database Tools from version 3.1.4 through versions before 100.20.1.

descriptions.value: CakePHP 4.5.12, 4.6.5, 5.1.8 through 5.1.10, 5.2.14 through 5.2.15, 5.3.7, and 5.4.0 through 5.4.3 contain an email header injection vulnerability because SmtpTransport and MailTransport strip only CRLF pairs from header values, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-77634. descriptions.value: Pi-hole is a DNS sinkhole that protects devices from unwanted content without installing any client-side software. Prior to 6.5, advanced/Scripts/utils.sh getFTLPID() attempts to validate the pihole-owned /run/pihole-FTL.pid file with expr "${FTL_PID}" : "[^[:digit:]]", but this rejects only values whose first character is not a digit. An attacker with code execution as the pihole user can write a digit-prefixed arithmetic expression to the pihole-owned PID file. Root-run pihole subcommands then evaluate [[ "$pid" -eq "-1" ]], causing Bash to recursively evaluate array subscripts and execute command substitution as root. cna.title: Next.js: Cache poisoning of shared fallback shells in Cache Components via request-supplied placeholder route params

descriptions.value: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.4.0 until 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js applications served with next start can allow an unauthenticated request to poison a shared fallback shell when cacheComponents is true and partialPrefetching is unset or false. The affected dynamic route must have a prerenderable param declared by generateStaticParams whose requested value was not generated at build time, at least two never-prerenderable params below it, a layout that reads the shallower param inside a Suspense boundary, and a blocking fallback shell. A request-supplied placeholder route param whose path segment equals the percent-encoded bracketed name of its own deeper route param is incorrectly treated as unresolved, while the shallower concrete value is rendered into the shared shell and its HTTP status is persisted. Depending on application behavior, subsequent routes sharing that shell can receive a persistent 404 or attacker-selected substituted param text. Client hydration corrects substituted text, and the issue does not enable markup or script injection or disclose data. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

references.name: Information disclosure in `AshAi.ToToolError` in AshAi sends raw exception text to tool callers

descriptions.value:
Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in ash-project ash_ai allows a caller of an AshAi tool to read internal error details, including module names and data values, by making a tool call fail.

AshAi.ToToolError gained an implementation for Ash.Error.Unknown.UnknownError that returns the error's error field as is, and AshAi.Tool.Errors.format/1 sends that text to MCP clients (tool calls and resource reads in AshAi.Mcp.Server) and to the model in AshAi.ToolLoop. Ash stores the full Exception.format/2 output of a raised exception, or inspect/1 of a bare {:error, term} return, in that field. A tool result that cannot be JSON-encoded raises a Protocol.UndefinedError whose text includes the inspected value, which can be a whole record with fields the tool never returns. None of these errors were logged. The fix logs them under an error id and returns only that id to the caller.

This issue affects ash_ai: from 1.5.0 before 1.5.1.

descriptions.value: Nx is a monorepo solution for TypeScript and polyglot codebases. From 22.0.2 until 22.7.9 and 23.1.2 for @nx/maven, and from 21.0.0 until 22.7.9 and 23.1.2 for @nx/gradle, the plugins' project-graph analyzers launch through a shell and interpolate plugin options from nx.json into command arguments. cna.title: TYPO3 CMS - Missing Authorization in Online Media Handling

descriptions.value:
The backend endpoint for adding online media (e.g. YouTube or Vimeo videos) accepted a target folder in the fallback storage (storage uid 0), which points to the public web root of the installation. File mount and permission checks are not applied to the fallback storage. As a result, any authenticated, low-privileged backend user, even without file mounts or module access, could create online media files with a partially controllable file name in the public web root.

In combination with TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-027, this could be used to re-enable the installer on an already configured instance. The installer could then be used to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH RTP Inject and RTP Bleed during auto adjustment, plus SRTP media denial of service

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. In 1.11.2 and earlier, rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c uses one session-wide autoadj_tally to learn RTP sources that differ from the address negotiated in SDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker who sends plaintext RTP during call setup can make packets from one or more non-advertised sources reach the threshold before the legitimate endpoint, causing FreeSWITCH to adopt the source of the threshold-crossing packet as the media peer. The attacker can then receive call audio, inject media, and deny media to the legitimate endpoint without being on the media path. FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 adds two opt-in controls, but both default to zero and the release remains affected unless both are configured before RTP session creation. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.11.2.

cna.title: Immich: A regular user can create SharedLink for album/asset belonging to another user through CreateSharedLink API

descriptions.value: Immich is a high-performance self-hosted photo and video management solution. Prior to 3.2.0, the shared-link creation API accepted albumId and assetIds as independent fields in server/src/services/shared-link.service.ts but authorized only the resource selected by the requested link type. workarounds.value: Replace calls to ezstd:decompress_using_ddict/2 with the streaming API: create a context with ezstd:create_decompression_context/1 using a small output buffer, attach the dictionary with ezstd:select_ddict/2, and decompress with ezstd:decompress_streaming/2. The streaming path decompresses into the caller-sized buffer and gives up with {error, decompressor_stuck} after 1000 chunks, so a 64 KiB buffer caps a single call at 64 MiB of output. Treat that error as a rejected input. Legitimate frames whose output exceeds 1000 times the buffer size fail the same way, so size the buffer for the largest expected payload.

descriptions.value:
Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in silviucpp ezstd allows an attacker who supplies a zstd frame to ezstd:decompress_using_ddict/2 to exhaust memory and terminate the Erlang VM via a small frame that declares a very large content size.

zstd_nif_decompress_using_ddict in c_src/ezstd_nif.cc reads the frame's declared content size with ZSTD_getFrameContentSize and passes it directly to enif_make_new_binary, without the 1 GiB MAX_BUFFER_SIZE check that ezstd:decompress/1 applies before allocating. A valid 65,550-byte frame of RLE blocks declaring 2 GiB is rejected by ezstd:decompress/1 but is fully allocated and decompressed by the dictionary path. The allocation happens inside a NIF, so when it exceeds the memory available to the VM the operating system kills the whole node rather than the calling process.

This issue affects ezstd: from 1.0.5 before 1.2.5.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* Build ezstd 1.2.4 and start a VM under an external memory limit, for example a container limited to 256 MiB.
* Create any decompression dictionary with ezstd:create_ddict/1; its content does not matter because the frame carries no dictionary ID.
* Construct a zstd frame: the magic number, a frame header descriptor selecting an 8-byte content size, a window descriptor, a little-endian content size of 2 GiB, then 16,383 RLE blocks of 128 KiB each (block header 0x02 0x00 0x10 followed by one payload byte) and a final RLE block with the last-block bit set. The frame is 65,550 bytes.
* Call ezstd:decompress/1 on the frame: it returns {error, <<"frame too large or invalid">>}.
* Call ezstd:decompress_using_ddict/2 on the same frame with the dictionary: the VM is killed by the operating system (exit status 137).
* Repeat on 1.2.5: the call returns {error, <<"frame too large or invalid">>} and the VM continues.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Declared size is attacker controlled. A zstd frame header carries an optional Frame Content Size field. zstd_nif_decompress_using_ddict in c_src/ezstd_nif.cc reads it with ZSTD_getFrameContentSize and rejects only the two sentinel values ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN and ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_ERROR.

2. Unbounded allocation. The size is passed directly to enif_make_new_binary, so a frame declaring 2 GiB makes the NIF request a 2 GiB binary. The sibling zstd_nif_decompress rejects any declared size above MAX_BUFFER_SIZE (1 GiB) before allocating; the dictionary path omitted that check from the commit that introduced it.

3. Amplification. A frame built from RLE blocks, each encoding 128 KiB of a repeated byte in four bytes, declares and genuinely decompresses to 2 GiB from 65,550 bytes of input, a ratio of about 32,760:1. ZSTD_decompress_usingDDict then fills the buffer. Because this happens inside a NIF, exceeding the memory available to the VM results in the operating system killing the whole BEAM process rather than an Erlang-level exception.

Declared size is attacker controlled.** A zstd frame header carries an optional Frame Content Size field. `zstd_nif_decompress_using_ddict` in `c_src/ezstd_nif.cc` reads it with `ZSTD_getFrameContentSize` and rejects only the two sentinel values `ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN` and `ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_ERROR`.

**2. Unbounded allocation.** The size is passed directly to `enif_make_new_binary`, so a frame declaring 2 GiB makes the NIF request a 2 GiB binary. The sibling `zstd_nif_decompress` rejects any declared size above `MAX_BUFFER_SIZE` (1 GiB) before allocating; the dictionary path omitted that check from the commit that introduced it.

**3. Amplification.** A frame built from RLE blocks, each encoding 128 KiB of a repeated byte in four bytes, declares and genuinely decompresses to 2 GiB from 65,550 bytes of input, a ratio of about 32,760:1. `ZSTD_decompress_usingDDict` then fills the buffer. Because this happens inside a NIF, exceeding the memory available to the VM results in the operating system killing the whole BEAM process rather than an Erlang-level exception.

cna.title: libp2p: gossipsub creates a permanent topics-map entry per distinct subscription with no cap in the default config

descriptions.value: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 17.0.0, the @libp2p/gossipsub default configuration allows a connected remote peer to submit unsigned subscription RPC metadata for arbitrarily many distinct topic strings. handleReceivedSubscription in packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts creates a persistent topics-map entry for each accepted topic, while allowedTopics is unset by default, decodeRpc maxSubscriptions limits only one RPC rather than aggregate topic bytes, and peer scoring has no subscription-volume penalty. A single peer can therefore grow the topics map and committed heap toward out-of-memory conditions, and disconnecting additionally causes removePeer to scan all accumulated topic entries. This issue is fixed in version 17.0.0.

A database user who can create and populate a suitably encoded collection can cause a later authorized directory restore to write those documents into a different collection that the user cannot modify directly. When both collection names resolve to the same destination, backed-up documents may be omitted; use of --drop can also replace the unintended destination collection. Exploitation requires an operator to restore the affected collection from a directory dump with write access to the destination. This issue affects MongoDB Database Tools versions 100.0.2 through versions before 100.20.1.

workarounds.value: Block untrusted H.264 RTP streams at the network perimeter (firewall or UDP ingress filter) to prevent malformed packets from reaching GStreamer pipelines. Alternatively, disable or avoid deploying the rtph264depay GStreamer element when processing RTP from untrusted sources.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-good, specifically in the H.264 RTP depayloader element. When processing MTAP16 or MTAP24 multi-time aggregation RTP packets, a signed/unsigned integer conversion error causes the remaining-length counter to underflow to a large positive value when the packet is truncated. This allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds heap read of up to approximately 64 KiB of process memory by sending a single malformed RTP packet. Successful exploitation can crash the receiving GStreamer pipeline (denial of service), and in relay or transcoding deployments where output is accessible to the attacker, may expose adjacent heap contents.

descriptions.value: Content Egg plugin for WordPress before 12.1.0 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve Content Egg product data from unpublished posts by calling the REST route POST /wp-json/content-egg/v1/render-blocks, whose permission_check() improperly returns true when no X-WP-Nonce header is supplied. cna.title: Immich: Unauthenticated filesystem path injection (arbitrary directory write + recursive delete) in the machine-learning service

descriptions.value: Immich is a high-performance self-hosted photo and video management solution. Prior to 3.3.0, the unauthenticated machine-learning /predict endpoint in machine-learning/immich_ml/main.py accepted an options object and passed its values into model construction in machine-learning/immich_ml/models/base.py without restricting security-sensitive parameters. An attacker with network access to the service could set cache_dir to an arbitrary writable path, causing model downloads to write there and causing clear_cache() to pass that path to shutil.rmtree() after selected model-loading failures. Depending on filesystem permissions and the selected path, this could modify files in mounted data locations or recursively delete an attacker-selected directory. The model-name allowlist prevents this issue from becoming arbitrary-model deserialization or code execution. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.0.

cna.title: pyasn1: Quadratic-complexity denial of service in binary REAL decoding

descriptions.value: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. Prior to 0.6.5, binary REAL decoding builds a large mantissa one octet at a time by shifting a growing integer and slicing the remaining byte string. Attacker-controlled ASN.1 includes a binary-encoded REAL with a large mantissa and reaches BER, CER, or DER decode(), with or without a schema containing REAL. RealPayloadDecoder.valueDecoder repeatedly performs a left shift, OR, and suffix copy for every mantissa octet, making decode time quadratic in mantissa length. A comparatively small REAL value can hold a decoding worker on one CPU core for seconds or longer and cause availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

cna.title: Zuke: githubWorkflow adopts any workflow run whose title matches its marker, so anyone who can dispatch the workflow can satisfy or block a release gate

descriptions.value: Zuke is a code-first, strongly typed build automation system for Deno. Prior to 1.10.0, the @zuke/gh githubWorkflow(...) gate correlates a dispatched workflow run using only a display-title marker that is visible in the workflow run list and can be copied by another dispatcher. In configurations where the external workflow repository grants workflow_dispatch permission to a party not equally trusted by the releasing repository, an attacker can dispatch a run with the marker and cause the gate to adopt its conclusion without verifying the event, ref, or creation window. A passing substituted run can authorize an unvalidated release, while a failed or cancelled run can block a valid release, and the persisted adopted run ID preserves the substitution across build resume. This issue is fixed in version 1.10.0.

cna.title: gopacket: SCTP chunk sub-decoder out-of-bounds panics on crafted segments

descriptions.value: gopacket provides packet processing capabilities for Go. Prior to 1.7.2, the SCTP chunk chain in layers/sctp.go passes attacker-controlled declared lengths and counts to decodeSCTPInit, decodeSCTPShutdown, decodeSCTPError, decodeSCTPSack, and decodeSCTPParameter without checking that each chunk contains the fixed fields, parameter TLVs, gap acknowledgements, or duplicate TSNs those sub-decoders read. A crafted SCTP segment can therefore cause out-of-bounds or inverted slice panics; the panic can terminate applications that use gopacket.DecodeOptions.SkipDecodeRecovery, direct registered decoders, or DecodingLayerParser with IgnorePanic enabled, while the default recovery-enabled APIs convert it to a per-packet decode error. This is the SCTP sub-decoder residual named but not remediated by CVE-2026-65819, whose version 1.7.1 changes bounded the generic dispatcher but left these per-type reads and loops unchecked. The impact is availability only, with no data disclosure, modification, or allocation amplification. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.2.

cna.title: Krb5: mit krb5 kdc unauthenticated cpu dos via quadratic asn.1 sequence of decoding

credits.value: This issue was discovered by AISLE Research and Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat.

affected.product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 Extended Update Support
Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support

workarounds.value:
Restrict incoming TCP traffic on port 88 to trusted internal networks or authorized administrative hosts using firewalld.

1. Add a rich rule permitting TCP port 88 only from trusted networks (substitute with the appropriate network CIDR):
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" port port="88" protocol="tcp" accept'

2. Ensure unauthenticated or public access to port 88/tcp is removed:
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=88/tcp

3. Apply the changes:
firewall-cmd --reload

Warning: Applying firewall changes requires reloading firewalld, which may temporarily disrupt network traffic. Restricting TCP access will prevent clients outside the allowed network range from falling back to TCP for large Kerberos ticket exchanges.

descriptions.value: decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded element array one entry at a time, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field over TCP.

cna.title: Registration Form for WooCommerce <= 1.1.4 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to 'user_roles' Parameter at Checkout

descriptions.value: The Registration Form for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to privilege escalation due to a missing allow-list check in the FormHandler::validate_checkout_fields() function in versions up to, and including, 1.1.4 The My Account registration path (validate_fields()) validates a submitted 'tgwcfb/user-roles' value against the form's configured allowed roles, but the checkout registration path (validate_checkout_fields(), hooked to woocommerce_after_checkout_validation) stores the raw $_POST['user_roles'] value in $this->valid_data without any allow-list enforcement, and add_user_data() then injects that value into woocommerce_new_customer_data as the new account's role. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to elevate their privileges to Administrator by supplying a user_roles=administrator parameter when creating an account during checkout, resulting in full site takeover.
