descriptions.value:
MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the default theme's Galaxies index page. When a MISP instance detects unknown custom or default galaxy clusters during synchronization, it renders sample tag names in an informational notice directed at site administrators. In the default theme, these sample tag names were inserted into the HTML output without HTML-entity encoding. A user with tag-editor privileges could craft a malicious misp-galaxy tag containing arbitrary script. When a site administrator subsequently viewed the Galaxies index page, the crafted tag content was interpreted as executable markup in the administrator's browser session, enabling the attacker to read session data, perform actions on behalf of the administrator, or otherwise compromise the administrator's browser context. The Overmind theme already applied HTML escaping to the same values and was not affected. The vulnerability requires the attacker to possess tag-editor-level access to create the crafted tag and requires the victim (a site administrator) to view the Galaxies index page in the default theme. The impact is limited to the administrator's browser session and does not directly compromise the MISP server process.

Version affected: <2.5.47

cna.title: Net::LibSSH versions before 0.004 for Perl authenticate to an unverified server because connect never checks the host key against known_hosts

solutions.value: Upgrade to Net-LibSSH 0.004 or later.

descriptions.value:
Net::LibSSH versions before 0.004 for Perl authenticate to an unverified server because connect never checks the host key against known_hosts.

connect reports success as soon as ssh_connect returns SSH_OK. libssh leaves the known-hosts check to the application, and this binding never makes it, so the strict_hostkeycheck and knownhosts options are set on the session and then decide nothing.

Password, agent and public-key authentication, channel and SFTP operations all run on a session whose peer was never identified, so an attacker who can redirect the connection receives the password when password authentication is used, and commands and data sent over the session.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the authentication session management of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when an administrator enforces a stronger authentication flow, such as mandatory two-factor authentication (2FA) setup, through a client policy. A user can bypass this requirement by manually visiting a specific session restart web link during the login process. This action clears the internal markers that track the required security steps, allowing the user to log in with only a password and gain access without completing the mandated 2FA setup.

cna.title: MISP: HTTP Method Bypass of Login Security Controls (Bruteforce Protection and Email OTP)

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [security] insufficient check on http methods for the

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [security] insufficient check on http methods for the
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix replaces the allowlist-style HTTP method checks (is POST or PUT) with a denylist approach (is NOT GET) in all three security-critical branches of the login() function. This ensures that every non-GET HTTP method—regardless of whether it is POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, or any other—triggers the bruteforce protection, email OTP verification, and login-failure logging code paths, closing the method-based bypass.
assumptions: The exact affected version range is not explicitly stated in the patch; the tag_version_boundary metadata indicates v2.5.47 with 143 commits after the fix, suggesting the fix landed shortly after 2.5.47, but the precise last-affected and first-fixed versions are not confirmed.

The CAPEC-1 mapping is the closest available pattern; the actual attack vector (HTTP method substitution) is a form of request parameter manipulation that does not have a dedicated CAPEC entry, so CAPEC-1 is used as the best approximation.
The CVSS vector assumes the MISP instance is exposed over a network and that the login endpoint is reachable without prior authentication, which is the standard deployment model for MISP.
The patch does not include a test case demonstrating the bypass; the analysis is based solely on the code diff and commit message.

It is assumed that the MISP framework (CakePHP) does not independently enforce HTTP method restrictions at a middleware layer that would have already blocked non-POST/PUT methods to this endpoint; the patch implies such enforcement was absent.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: Three conditional expressions in UsersController::login() were changed. (1) The bruteforce-protection guard changed from $this->request->is(['post','put']) to !$this->request->is(['get']). (2) The email-OTP guard changed from $this->request->is('post') to !$this->request->is(['get']). (3) The login-failure handling guard changed from $this->request->is('post') || $this->request->is('put') to !$this->request->is('get'). All three changes invert the logic from an explicit allowlist of methods to a denylist that excludes only GET, so that any other HTTP method is treated as a state-changing login attempt subject to all security controls.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N – the login endpoint is network-accessible. AC:L – the attack requires only changing the HTTP method in a request; no race conditions or complex setup. AT:N – no manipulation of the target system is needed. PR:N – the login endpoint is accessible without prior authentication. UI:N – no user interaction required. VC:L – bypass of bruteforce protection enables credential brute-forcing, potentially exposing user credentials. VI:L – bypass of email OTP (2FA) and failure logging compromises the integrity of the authentication process and audit trail. VA:N – no direct denial-of-service impact. SC/SI/SA:N – no secondary system impact is evidenced.

capecRationale.rationale: The attacker modifies a parameter of the authentication request (the HTTP method) to alter which security checks are executed, effectively modifying the authentication logic at runtime. This is the closest CAPEC to the observed bypass. Uncertainty: CAPEC-1 typically refers to modifying authentication logic in a more direct sense (e.g., altering credential checks), whereas here the modification is via the HTTP method header. However, no other CAPEC more precisely captures the act of altering a request attribute to skip authentication security controls.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The root cause is that the application validated the HTTP method using an incomplete allowlist (POST, PUT) rather than rejecting all non-safe methods. This is a classic improper input validation flaw where the set of accepted values was not exhaustive, allowing unexpected methods to bypass security logic.

The security controls (bruteforce protection, OTP enforcement, failure logging) are authorization/authentication enforcement mechanisms that were improperly applied only to a subset of HTTP methods, effectively allowing unauthorized bypass of these controls.

descriptions.value:
The login() function in MISP's UsersController.php contained insufficient HTTP method validation for several security-critical code paths. The original code used an allowlist approach, checking only for specific HTTP methods (POST and PUT) before enforcing bruteforce protection, email one-time-password (OTP) verification, and login-failure logging. Because the checks were not exhaustive, an unauthenticated attacker could issue login requests using other HTTP methods and bypass all three security controls simultaneously. Specifically: 

 - the bruteforce blocklisting check and attempt counter were skipped, allowing unlimited credential-guessing attempts without being rate-limited or blocked
 -  the email OTP two-factor authentication step was skipped, defeating the second factor of authentication
 - login-failure events were neither logged nor counted, removing the audit trail and the mechanism that would normally trigger a blocklist entry.




The security impact is the effective disabling of brute-force protection and multi-factor authentication for any attacker who can craft an HTTP request with a non-POST/PUT method to the login endpoint, potentially leading to credential compromise and unauthorized access to the MISP instance.





Version affected: <2.5.47

cna.title: Authorization: Negotiate sent to foreign origin

descriptions.value:
When processing an HTTP redirect to a URL containing userinfo (a
`username:password` component), curl might erroneously retain and re-transmit
the original host's HTTP Negotiate authentication state. Consequently, a
malicious server can trigger a redirect containing arbitrary userinfo to force
curl to send a freshly minted Kerberos ticket—generated using the ambient
identity of the client process to an untrusted third-party host, effectively
bypassing the domain-scoping restrictions normally enforced by the absence of
`--location-trusted`.

cna.title: Apache MINA SSHD: Memory exhaustion in SFTP client via unsolicited SFTP replies

descriptions.value:
Possible memory exhaustion in SFTP clients (DefaultSftpClient) in component sshd-sftp in Apache MINA SSHD versions 0.9.0 to 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5.




Apache 
MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH. The sshd-sftp component provides support for SFTP.




The SFTP client implementation, when receiving a reply, did not check that this reply corresponded to a request sent earlier. Unsolicited replies would be stored but never consumed. A malicious server could keep sending unsolicited replies until available memory in the client was exhausted.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue.

cna.title: NukeVie: Login Lockout Bypass via Untrusted Forwarded-IP Headers

descriptions.description: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

descriptions.value: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can rotate X-Forwarded-For because vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Ips.php accepts forwarded client-IP headers without first confirming that REMOTE_ADDR is a trusted proxy. The resulting NV_CLIENT_IP keys the administrator login blocker in includes/core/admin_login.php; changing only the header value bypasses that lockout and permits effectively unlimited password guesses. The same spoofable address is also consumed by the user login blocker in modules/users/funcs/login.php, IP restrictions, bans, flood controls, and security logs, but those additional code-level effects were not dynamically demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

cna.title: Unauthenticated recovery of the Math.random() state behind OAuth tokens, authorization codes, client secrets and organization API keys

descriptions.value: An unauthenticated attacker who predicts an OAuth access token minted for another organization is authenticated as that organization with SUPERADMIN rights over the public API, giving full read and write access to its scheduled posts, connected social accounts, media and team membership.

The per-organization API key generated at registration is drawn from the same generator and is honoured by the same middleware with the same SUPERADMIN grant, so an attacker sampling the generator around a signup can predict the API key of a newly created organization.

OAuth client secrets, including those returned by anonymous dynamic client registration and by secret rotation, are predictable, allowing an attacker to impersonate a registered OAuth or MCP client to the token endpoint.
Authorization codes issued at the consent step are predictable, exposing in-flight OAuth authorization flows to interception and redemption by a third party.
PKCE code verifiers generated for social account connections are predictable, removing the protection PKCE is present to provide for those provider flows.

exploits.value: No public exploit code is known. The original submission was methodology-only and deliberately omitted a working implementation.

timeline.value: Postiz has received and acknowledged the report.
Postiz has developed and verified the patch.
Postiz has released the patch notes and published the advisory.

solutions.value: Run a Postiz release in which security-sensitive identifiers are generated from a cryptographically secure random source rather than from Math.random(). No fixed release is available at the time of writing; this advisory will record the fixed version once one is published.

Once running a release with a corrected generator, treat every credential issued by an affected version as compromised and replace it. That covers organization API keys, OAuth application client secrets, and any outstanding OAuth access tokens and authorizations. Outstanding authorization codes are short-lived and expire on their own.
Operators who connected social accounts while running an affected version should review those connections, since the PKCE verifiers used to establish them were drawn from the same generator.

workarounds.value: Blocking or requiring authentication on the OAuth dynamic client registration endpoint at a reverse proxy, gateway or WAF removes the anonymous bulk-sampling surface, which is the part of this issue reachable without an account. It does not make the generated values unpredictable, and it does not close the surfaces available to an authenticated user, so it narrows exposure rather than resolving it. Deployments that do not use OAuth or MCP client integrations can apply this with no loss of function.

Rotating organization API keys or OAuth client secrets while still running an affected version does not help, and should not be relied on as a mitigation. The replacement value is produced by the same generator and is predictable on the same terms as the value it replaces. Rotation is only meaningful once the generator itself no longer draws from Math.random().

Where the deployment allows it, restricting the public API to known client networks limits who can present a predicted credential. This is a containment measure for the consequence rather than a fix for the predictability.

descriptions.value:
Postiz generates security-sensitive credentials using `Math.random()` instead of a cryptographically secure source. The same helper is used for OAuth access tokens, authorization codes, client secrets, organization API keys, and PKCE verifiers, meaning these credentials depend entirely on V8’s deterministic xorshift128+ PRNG state.

An unauthenticated OAuth dynamic client registration endpoint exposes freshly generated client credentials, giving attackers enough consecutive PRNG output to reconstruct that internal state. Once recovered, they can deterministically derive past and future values produced by the same generator, potentially compromising credentials belonging to other users and organizations.

configurations.value: All deployments running the released code up to and including v2.23.0 are affected, self-hosted and hosted alike. The identifier helper is shared code reached by every credential-minting path, and there is no feature flag, environment variable or build option that selects a different random source.

The anonymous sampling surface, the OAuth dynamic client registration endpoint, is registered in both the default controller set and the MCP_ONLY controller set, so it is reachable in either deployment mode.

cna.title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: Hard-coded root password on the serial console

credits.value: Llorenç Romá Alvarez, Security Researcher, Cyber Defence Campus, Switzerland

scenarios.value: Scored on the only login channel that accepts the credential: the board's serial console, which requires physical access, so AV:P. No network login service (SSH/telnet) runs on the board by default. The credential is not an escalation on a host where code execution has already been achieved. BLAST RADIUS: the credential is image-wide, not per-device, so a single recovery applies to every affected unit and an operator cannot contain a leak. The vendor should also determine whether the same credential is reused in other DJI product lines; reuse was not verified in this engagement.

modules: 1300 DM810X communications board (uavmonitor_usbv1; root console credential in /etc/shadow)

timeline.value: DJI acknowledged the vulnerability and provided its assessment

solutions.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

supportingMedia.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

references.name: DJI AeroScope Mobile research repository (technical details)

workarounds.value: Restrict physical access to deployed units and their serial console, and treat any unit that has left controlled custody as having a known root password. Network isolation does not mitigate this issue.

supportingMedia.value: Restrict physical access to deployed units and their serial console, and treat any unit that has left controlled custody as having a known root password. Network isolation does not mitigate this issue.

descriptions.value:
Use of hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) on the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an attacker with physical access to the board's serial console to log in as root. The same password hash is present on every unit and uses DES crypt, so the password can be recovered offline from the distributed firmware. No network login service accepts this password by default. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

cna.title: envd: Host file disclosure through requirements path traversal and TOCTOU

descriptions.value: envd provides reproducible development environments for humans and agents. In versions starting with 0.3.38 and before 1.3.6, insufficient containment of host-side requirements-file reads in  install.python_packages(requirements=...)  could allow access to files outside the build context. An attacker able to influence build input could cause file contents interpreted as dependency entries to appear in debug logs or build-step metadata, subject to the envd process’s permissions. descriptions.value: When Gitea acts as an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider, the token endpoint did not check the state of the user. descriptions.value: An authenticated user with a pending or declined group invitation carrying share_admin=True can delete the group's share-right records, revoking that group's access to the affected shares and their contained secrets for all accepted group members. scenarios.value: Authenticated user with a pending or declined group invitation carrying share_admin=True and knowledge of a target group share-right UUID. Unauthorized deletion modifies access-control records and removes the group's access to affected shared data.

solutions.value: Upgrade Psono Server Community Edition and Psono Server Enterprise Edition to version 7.5.1 or later. Version 7.5.1 was released for both editions on 2026-10-13. descriptions.value: Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition before 7.5.1 do not require accepted group membership when authorizing deletion of group share-rights. Pending invitations have accepted=None, while declined invitations retain accepted=False and the share_admin flag. cna.title: Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext

descriptions.value: CAPEC-158 Sniffing Network Traffic

Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: gittuf: Propagated controller policies not loaded during verification

solutions.value: Upgrade to gittuf 0.18.0 or later, then run gittuf verify-ref over the full history of each protected reference. Policy propagation has been moved back into gittuf's developer mode.

descriptions.value: In gittuf 0.10.0 through 0.17.0, the verification workflow does not load policy updates that are propagated from an upstream (controller) repository and recorded in the reference state log after the first entry being verified. credits.value: Llorenç Romá Alvarez, Security Researcher, Cyber Defence Campus, Switzerland

scenarios.value: Primary score assumes Adjacent (AV:A) reach via the L2 multicast arming handshake. If the management interface is IP-routed/bridged, the TCP 16000 firmware-flash dispatch is reachable at Network scope: use AV:N -> CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H = 9.8 CRITICAL.

timeline.value: Reproduced in emulation of the unmodified device binaries
DJI acknowledged the vulnerability and provided its assessment

solutions.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

workarounds.value: Connect the unit's management Ethernet port only to an isolated network segment with no untrusted hosts, and do not route or bridge that segment to other networks, so that TCP port 16000 and the multicast discovery traffic (225.0.0.37, UDP port 16001) cannot be reached. The device has no setting that enables signature checking of firmware updates.

cna.title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request replay and buffer growth behind a declined upgrade

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, when the pipelined request queue is full, the pure-Python parser stores the unparsed remainder internally and also returns the same data to its caller. After a handler declines an upgrade request, the caller feeds the remainder back to the parser, causing the buffer to grow with each handled request and dispatching already-handled requests to the application again. The issue affects deployments using AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS or otherwise running without the standard C-extension wheel, and can cause excessive memory use and repeated request processing. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: Kroxylicious-authorizer-acl: kroxylicious: acl rule file regex escapes are stripped, broadening 'matching' authorization rules

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Carles Arnal (IBM) for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Until a fixed release is available, write regex escapes with doubled backslashes (for example `/orders\\.v1/`), audit existing `matching` rules for unintended matches, and prefer exact or `like` predicates where regex matching is not required.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Kroxylicious. The ACL authorizer's rules-file parser unquotes `matching /…/` regular-expression literals using the string unquoting rules, which strips every backslash escape. As a result, an allow rule such as `matching /orders\.v1/` is compiled as the regex `orders.v1`, which also matches unintended names such as `ordersXv1`, and character classes such as `\d` and `\w` lose their special meaning. Allow rules written with regex escapes can therefore apply to more resources than the author intended. Depending on the ACL configuration, this may allow an authenticated Kafka client to access a resource (such as read or write a topic) that should have been denied.

cna.title: AIOHTTP: Base64 multipart parts bypass client_max_size

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, BodyPartReader.read_chunk() processing a multipart part with Content-Transfer-Encoding set to base64 keeps reading until the chunk length is a multiple of four without enforcing a byte limit. A short Content-Length or a long run of whitespace can cause one call to read the remaining body into memory before the size check or spin on the event loop. A remote attacker can send such a multipart request to a handler that reads multipart data and bypass client_max_size. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: Apache SeaTunnel Web: Disabled accounts can obtain new login tokens

descriptions.value:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** 



Improper Authentication in Apache SeaTunnel Web 1.0.2 allows a user whose account has been disabled to authenticate with valid credentials and obtain a new login token. The login query does not check the account status, so disabling an account does not prevent new logins or access to protected APIs using the newly issued token. This issue requires valid credentials for the disabled account; it is not a credential-free authentication bypass.

cna.title: AES key schedule not cleared by the TinyCrypt AES-CTR backend in MCUboot bootutil

descriptions.value:
When MCUboot is built with the TinyCrypt crypto backend (MCUBOOT_USE_TINYCRYPT), bootutil_aes_ctr_drop() in boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/aes_ctr_tinycrypt.h was an empty stub. The AES-CTR context for this backend is the fully expanded AES-128 key schedule (struct tc_aes_key_sched_struct). Generic code relies on this hook to release and clear key state, so with TinyCrypt nothing was cleared. The mbedTLS and PSA backends do free or destroy their key state here.

As a result, boot_state_clear(), which boot_go() calls before handing off to the application, left the image's AES content-encryption key schedule in the static boot_data state. This is the case after an encrypted upgrade in single-image builds, where boot_enc_zeroize() is not called. boot_decrypt_key() likewise left the ECIES-derived key-encryption key schedule on the stack. The affected build uses MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES with TinyCrypt, which is the default ECDSA and Ed25519 backend in the Zephyr port.

The first AES-128 round key equals the cipher key, so anyone who can read the leftover bootloader RAM after boot can recover the image content key and decrypt that encrypted image. That includes a physical attacker with debug or RAM access, or code later running on the device. This weakens image-encryption key confidentiality (and so the confidentiality of the encrypted image's plaintext). The device's long-term private decryption key is not exposed, and image authenticity is not affected. The fix wipes the context with bootutil_wipe_memory().

cna.title: Nuxt payload URL generation has quadratic cost for repeated slashes in the request path

descriptions.value: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, _payload.json URL generation and the experimental early-404 path use a trailing-slash regular expression whose work grows quadratically with a long run of slash characters. An unauthenticated request can synchronously occupy the Node.js event loop and delay other requests when server-side rendering uses isr, swr, or cache route rules, or when experimental.early404 is enabled. Applications without those route rules and without experimental.early404, fully prerendered applications, and client-only applications are unaffected; the impact is limited to availability. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

cna.title: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for GHSA-6gq8-jgmh-3ffp: an encoded slash (`%2F`) in the request path bypasses route rules on catch-all page routes

descriptions.value: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. Nuxt from 3.0.0 until 4.6.4, @nuxt/nitro-server from 3.20.0 until 4.6.4, and @nuxt/vite-server from 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, routeRules matching leaves an encoded slash (%2F) in the request path while a catch-all page such as app/pages/[...slug].vue or a custom multi-segment page route decodes it into a route parameter. The getRouteRules result is therefore incomplete, and an unauthenticated request can render the page without the redirect, headers, proxy, SSR, noScripts, appMiddleware, or appLayout rules configured for the decoded path. Protected content is resolved only when the page interprets the decoded parameter accordingly: a custom multi-segment parameter can contain the decoded path, while a repeatable catch-all must join the slash-containing array element; route.path remains encoded and does not resolve that resource. Static pages, single-segment parameters, server/api handlers, and server/routes handlers are not affected because they do not have the same encoded-path mismatch. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

cna.title: SvelteKit: Protocol-relative module import during server-side route resolution allows cross-origin script execution

descriptions.value: SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. Prior to versions 2.70.4 and 3.1.1, apps configured with router.resolution: 'server' could treat a pathname beginning with // as a protocol-relative module specifier during client-side navigation. A socially engineered link could therefore make server-side route resolution import and execute JavaScript from another origin in the user's browser. This issue is fixed in 2.70.4 and 3.1.1.

cna.title: opentelemetry-go: AttributeValueLengthLimit is fully bypassed by attribute values composed of valid U+FFFD runes

descriptions.value: OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From SDK version 1.33.0, SDK log version 0.9.0, and trace version 1.35.0 until version 1.47.0, the AttributeValueLengthLimit and WithAttributeValueLengthLimit truncation paths in sdk/internal/attrnorm, sdk/log/internal/attrnorm, and trace/auto.go do not count valid U+FFFD replacement characters. cna.title: dnspython excessive memory and CPU use

descriptions.value: dnspython is a DNS toolkit for Python. An attacker-controlled zone file can supply a larger number, causing the service bitmap to grow to an extremely large size through inefficient repeated extension, consuming excessive memory and CPU and potentially terminating the process. cna.title: Nuxt: Colliding island props can share one `/__nuxt_island` path (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-46342)

descriptions.value: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.21.6 to before 4.0.0 and from 4.4.6 until 4.6.4, the /__nuxt_island path hash uses ohash serialization that does not escape quotes in string values or delimiters in object keys, allowing different island-prop tuples to produce the same path. For prerendering, substituted content is written into the generated page only if the crawler reaches a colliding URL before rendering the page with the legitimate props. Separately, a CDN or reverse proxy that keys island responses by path alone can be primed with the colliding response. If the substituted prop reaches v-html, innerHTML, or another unsafe HTML sink, the response can execute script in the application origin; otherwise the impact is content substitution. Applications that do not use server components or NuxtIsland, islands without attacker-influenced string props, and responses not cached by path alone are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

cna.title: gittuf: File protection rules bypassed for filenames with special characters

solutions.value: Upgrade to gittuf 0.18.0 or later, which asks Git for raw paths. Then re-run verification (gittuf verify-ref) for each protected reference: a reference that passed verification before the upgrade but fails after it contains a change that should have been blocked.

descriptions.value: In gittuf before 0.18.0, verification of file protection rules uses the quoted, escaped pathnames that Git prints by default for files with special characters (for example non-ASCII characters) instead of the raw paths. Such paths do not match patterns like file:internal/*, so the files are treated as unprotected, and a user who is not authorized by a file protection rule can change a protected file whose name contains special characters and still pass verification.

cna.title: NLTK corpus-reader view methods bypass the scoped root sandbox via intermediate-directory symlinks

descriptions.description: CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

descriptions.value: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 until 3.10.4, NLTK corpus-reader path pointers and view methods validate a requested relative path without consistently resolving intermediate directory symlinks against the reader's scoped root. A local attacker who can place such a symlink can make abspaths or words reach a readable file outside the corpus root and disclose its contents. On releases with pathsec enforcement, the file must remain inside a global NLTK allowed root; version 3.9.4 has enforcement disabled and permits a broader escape. cna.title: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-119200: a leading `//` in the request path bypasses `server/middleware` path checks and server route rules on page routes

descriptions.value: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, Nuxt parses a request path beginning with // as a URL host before rendering a page, while Nitro server/middleware and routeRules continue to evaluate the original path. An unauthenticated request such as //x/admin can therefore resolve to the /admin page without route-scoped serverHandlers, server/middleware path checks, redirects, or security headers configured for /admin. API handlers in server/api and server/routes, appMiddleware, page middleware are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

CAPEC-1

In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment do not apply an access rule's `FILTERLIST` fragment filters to single Submodel reads.



`GET /submodels` removes the fields that a rule's `FILTERLIST` hides, but `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}` and `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$metadata` return them unfiltered. An authenticated caller with READ access to a Submodel can therefore read fields that the access rules hide from them, for example `supplementalSemanticIds` keys that name the other parties allowed to read the Submodel.



If versioning is enabled (`history.mode` set to `api` or `audit`), `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$history` and `GET /shells/{aasIdentifier}/$history` in the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment return the complete stored version without applying the rule's formula or fragment filters. A caller whose rules grant READ on these routes can read fields that the access rules hide, and Submodels and Asset Administration Shells that the direct read does not return to them at all.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

cna.title: russh kex_done: shared-secret callback runs before server host-key verification

descriptions.value: russh is a Rust SSH client and server library that includes an SSH agent protocol implementation. From version 0.55.0 until version 0.65.1, the initial key exchange invokes client::Handler::kex_done() with the raw shared secret before check_server_key() accepts the server host key or certificate. A malicious SSH server can therefore trigger application-defined secondary-channel initialization or early data handling even when the server identity is subsequently rejected. Ordinary clients that keep the callback's no-op default or independently defer callback-derived actions until trust is confirmed are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.65.1.

cna.title: Open Redirect in MISP Modules Website Login via Unvalidated next Parameter

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [website] restrict post-login redirects to local paths

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [website] restrict post-login redirects to local paths
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix introduces a _safe_next_url() validation function that restricts post-login redirect destinations to local paths or same-host HTTP(S) URLs. Any target that is empty, contains backslashes, control characters, leading/trailing whitespace, an unrecognized scheme, a mismatched host, or a protocol-relative form is rejected and the user is redirected to the home page (/). Accepted same-host URLs are normalized to local paths (scheme and authority stripped) while preserving query strings and fragments, ensuring the Location header always contains a relative path. This eliminates the ability to redirect users to arbitrary external destinations after authentication.
assumptions: No specific affected or fixed version is identified in the patch metadata; the version range is recorded as unspecified.

The CVSS UI metric is set to Active (A) on the assumption that the victim must click a crafted link and submit login credentials; if the login page is auto-submitted in a phishing context, UI could be argued as Passive, but the evidence supports Active.
SC is set to Low based on the phishing/social-engineering risk of redirecting a user to an external site after login; no direct data exfiltration mechanism is present in the vulnerable code path.
The CAPEC-113 mapping is the closest available pattern for open redirect; no more specific CAPEC exists for post-login redirect manipulation.
The patch does not indicate whether this vulnerability was reported through a coordinated disclosure process; no finder or reporter credit is assigned beyond the remediation developer.
The website component is assumed to be a Flask-based web application served over HTTP(S); the patch does not specify deployment topology or additional authentication layers.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In website/app/account/account.py, the import of urlsplit and urlunsplit from urllib.parse is added. A new _safe_next_url() function is defined that validates the target string against a series of safety checks (whitespace, backslashes, control characters, scheme allowlist, host match, protocol-relative rejection, double-slash path rejection) and returns either a normalized local path or the fallback '/'. The login() handler's redirect call is changed from redirect(request.args.get('next') or '/') to redirect(_safe_next_url(request.args.get('next'))). A new test file website/tests/login_checks.py (172 lines) is added with comprehensive unit tests covering external rejection, malformed input rejection, local path preservation, same-host-with-port normalization, wrong-password non-redirect, CSRF enforcement, and remember-me cookie preservation. The website README is updated to document the new redirect validation behavior.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: exploitable over the network via a crafted URL. AC:L: no race conditions or special conditions; simply append a next parameter. AT:N: no attack requirements beyond delivering the URL. PR:N: the attacker needs no account; the victim performs the login. UI:A: the victim must actively visit the crafted URL and submit credentials. VC/VI/VA:N: the vulnerable system itself suffers no direct confidentiality, integrity, or availability loss. SC:L: subsequent confidentiality impact is low because the redirected user may be tricked into entering sensitive data on a phishing page, but the session cookie is domain-scoped and not directly exfiltrated. SI/SA:N: no subsequent integrity or availability impact is evidenced.

capecRationale.rationale: The patch directly addresses an open redirect: an attacker crafts a login URL with a malicious next parameter to redirect the victim to an external phishing site after authentication. CAPEC-113 describes exactly this attack pattern where a web application redirects to a user-controlled destination without proper validation. This is the closest and most precise CAPEC mapping available for this vulnerability class.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The login endpoint accepted an unvalidated user-supplied URL in the next query parameter and used it directly as the redirect destination, allowing an attacker to redirect authenticated users to arbitrary external sites. This is a textbook open redirect (CWE-601).

solutions.value: The fix introduces a _safe_next_url() validation function that restricts post-login redirect destinations to local paths or same-host HTTP(S) URLs. Any target that is empty, contains backslashes, control characters, leading/trailing whitespace, an unrecognized scheme, a mismatched host, or a protocol-relative form is rejected and the user is redirected to the home page (/). Accepted same-host URLs are normalized to local paths (scheme and authority stripped) while preserving query strings and fragments, ensuring the Location header always contains a relative path. descriptions.value: The MISP Modules website component contains an open redirect vulnerability in its login endpoint. The /login route accepted a user-supplied next query parameter and passed it directly to Flask's redirect() function without validating the destination. An attacker could craft a URL such as https://victim-host/login?next=https://attacker.example/phish and deliver it to a user (e.g., via email or a lookalike page). After the user successfully authenticated, the application issued a 302 redirect to the attacker-controlled external URL. This enables phishing attacks where a user, believing they are still on the legitimate MISP Modules site, may enter additional credentials or sensitive information on the attacker's page. It can also be used to obscure the true destination of a link, bypassing user trust in the legitimate domain. The vulnerability requires the victim to interact with the crafted URL and complete a login, but no prior authentication or special configuration is needed on the attacker's side. The affected component is the website sub-project of misp-modules, specifically the account blueprint in website/app/account/account.py. No version boundaries are specified in the patch metadata.

cna.title: AIOHTTP: Concatenated compressed streams cause excessive CPU use

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, aiohttp decompresses each member of a payload containing many concatenated gzip, deflate, or zstd streams by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, causing quadratic CPU use. Empty members produce no output, so client_max_size and output backpressure do not limit the work. A remote attacker can block a server event loop with a crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message, and a malicious server can similarly block a client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 ReDoS via slideFormula Shared Formula Translation

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 ReDoS via slideFormula Shared Formula Translation

descriptions.value: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in slideFormula in lib/utils/shared-formula.js when translating shared formulas to child cells. Attackers can supply a crafted spreadsheet with very long master formulas, such as runs of hyphens, causing quadratic regex backtracking that blocks the Node.js event loop.

cna.title: sqlite3-ruby: SQL Query Truncation

descriptions.value: sqlite3 provides Ruby bindings for the SQLite3 embedded database. Prior to 2.10.2, sqlite3-ruby casts Ruby string lengths to int before passing SQL through Database#prepare, bound String or Blob values through Statement#bind_param, and String or Blob results from Ruby-defined SQL functions and aggregates through Database#create_function and Database#create_aggregate. On 64-bit platforms, a string of 4 GiB (2^32 bytes) or larger can wrap the length so SQLite processes only a prefix. A truncated SQL string can drop trailing clauses such as a WHERE condition, while a truncated bound value matters only when the application validated the full value before binding it. Exploitation requires the application and server to accept and retain the unusually large attacker-controlled string. cna.title: AutoMapper: Uncontrolled Recursion with Constructor Parameters

descriptions.value: AutoMapper is a convention-based object-object mapper in .NET. Prior to 15.1.4 and from 16.0.0 until 16.3.0, AutoMapper increments type depth only after creating the destination, so recursive mapping performed through constructor parameters occurs before MaxDepth is counted. Destinations built through positional records or other constructors, and recursive ConstructUsing mappings that call context.Mapper, can therefore bypass explicit MaxDepth values and the default limit of 64. Deep attacker-influenced input can throw an uncatchable StackOverflowException and terminate the process. This issue is fixed in versions 15.1.4 and 16.3.0.

solutions.value: Upgrade to gittuf 0.17.0 or later, then run gittuf verify-ref over the full history of each protected reference. If an intermediate policy is invalid, verification stops with an error; review the reference state log and repository audit logs to find out whether a user with write access tampered with the policy.

descriptions.value: In gittuf 0.4.0 through 0.16.0, when a policy update appears within the range of reference state log entries being verified, verification checks only the root of trust signatures of the new policy and not the signatures of its other metadata (rule files). A user trusted to push to the repository who bypasses gittuf policy apply and writes the policy reference and reference state log directly can make an invalid policy apply during verification, weakening or strengthening the rules for later changes. The update is still recorded in the reference state log.

cna.title: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to multipart file/field type confusion via chunk-dependent header parsing

descriptions.value: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 3.2.1 through 3.2.5, the parser can interpret the same multipart bytes differently depending on how they are split across socket reads: when the sequence that terminates a part's header block arrives split exactly at the configured header size limit, an off by one error drops the final header line, so a part declared as a binary file attachment is emitted as an ordinary text field instead of a file. A remote client controls both the multipart body and the header padding needed to reach the boundary and can influence segmentation, so an application that applies upload validation such as malware scanning or extension checks only to file events while trusting plain field values may process the payload through the wrong path. The parser level type confusion is fully reproducible, while the downstream validation bypass depends on the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which tracks how many terminator bytes were actually buffered when the limit is reached so a split terminator no longer corrupts the final header, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, apply the same validation to field values as to file uploads rather than treating file events as a trust boundary.

cna.title: rails-html-sanitizer: Possible XSS via shared scrubber state in concurrent calls

descriptions.value: rails-html-sanitizer is responsible for sanitizing HTML fragments in Rails applications. Before 1.7.2, the HTML4 and HTML5 variants of Rails::HTML::SafeListSanitizer reuse one Rails::HTML::PermitScrubber across calls and mutate its tags and attributes without synchronization. In a multithreaded process, concurrent sanitize calls using different tags: or attributes: options can interleave and cause one call to use the other call's allowlist. If a permissive call admits a script element or event-handler attribute, output expected to be sanitized under a stricter policy can retain it and cause cross-site scripting when rendered. Applications that are single-threaded, use one identical allowlist everywhere, or provide a separate scrubber: are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.2.

cna.title: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to Denial of Service via a multipart part with unterminated headers

descriptions.value: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, a multipart part whose header block is never terminated before the next boundary is counted by the vendored Dicer parser as an open part that never ends, so the parser emits neither a finish nor an error event and the request hangs. A single unauthenticated request of roughly one hundred bytes triggers the stall, and through @fastify/multipart the hung handler is not released when the client disconnects, so repeated requests leak handlers and whatever resources they hold, such as files, database connections and concurrency slots, until the process is restarted. The same parser is reached by the formData methods of undici versions 5.25.3 through 6.7.0. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, configure Fastify's handler timeout so hung handlers are eventually terminated and their resources released.

cna.title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow saving TIFF with libtiff when tags override image size

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.3.0 through 12.3.0, Pillow applications that save compressed TIFF images through libtiff can pass attacker-controlled image geometry tags to the encoder while allocating its row buffer from the actual image dimensions. The affected TiffImagePlugin._save path allows ImageWidth, ImageLength, or SamplesPerPixel from exif=, tiffinfo=, or a source TIFF IFD to make libtiff consume a larger scanline than the buffer supplied by ImagingLibTiffEncode. This can read heap memory into the generated TIFF or crash the process. When TIFF Predictor 2 is enabled, libtiff can rewrite the oversized scanline in place and corrupt memory beyond the buffer. A carried-over PlanarConfiguration value of 2 instead makes libtiff use a shorter scanline and can produce an undecodable output file, but is not established to cause the out-of-bounds access. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

descriptions.value: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.19.0 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in PayPal cancel and decline return handlers that trust only the checkout session without verifying the request came from PayPal. Attackers can lure a shopper into a cross-site GET to paypal/standard/cancel to cancel their recent uninvoiced order, void pending authorizations, and restore items to the cart.

cna.title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Prototype Pollution via x14 Conditional Formatting Rule ID

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Prototype Pollution via x14 Conditional Formatting Rule ID

descriptions.value: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in mergeConditionalFormattings that allows attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying an x14:cfRule id of __proto__. Attackers can craft an xlsx file that, when loaded with xlsx.load(), sets properties such as type, direction, border and cfvo on every object in the process until it restarts.

descriptions.description: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

cna.title: Scapy before 2.8.0 Uncontrolled Recursion DoS via BER SEQUENCE Decoder

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Scapy before 2.8.0 Uncontrolled Recursion DoS via BER SEQUENCE Decoder

descriptions.value: Scapy before 2.8.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in the BER/ASN.1 decoder in scapy/asn1/ber.py that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to crash parsing applications. Attackers can send a single 833-byte packet with 250 nested ASN.1 SEQUENCE structures to trigger an unhandled RecursionError, terminating TLS, SNMP, X.509, or LDAP parsers even with safe=True.

cna.title: NLTK dot2img runs Graphviz 'dot' without the trusted-exec chokepoint, enabling local code execution via a writable PATH element

descriptions.value: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img resolves the Graphviz dot executable through PATH but invokes the resulting absolute executable without routing through spawn_trusted, so resolve_trusted_executable ownership and writability validation and safe_env loader environment scrubbing do not run. A local low-privileged attacker who can write to a directory on a POSIX victim's PATH can plant or replace dot, and code executes as the victim when dot2img is called directly or DependencyGraph.repr_svg renders a graph. The current-working-directory-only bare-name vector is blocked and is not this vulnerability; this issue is the residual writable absolute PATH element bypass after CVE-2026-78680. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

cna.title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Memory Exhaustion via Oversized Image Anchor Column

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Memory Exhaustion via Oversized Image Anchor Column

descriptions.value: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a workbook with an unbounded image anchor column in the drawing part. Attackers can set an anchor column such as 300000000 in xl/drawings/drawing1.xml so reading getImages() anchor positions makes Worksheet.getColumn allocate millions of Column objects and abort with a heap out-of-memory error.

cna.title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: Missing authentication on the management interface

credits.value: Llorenç Romá Alvarez, Security Researcher, Cyber Defence Campus, Switzerland

scenarios.value: Score agreed with the vendor for the standalone impact of the interface. Adjacent (AV:A) reach via the multicast discovery on 225.0.0.37:16001. C:N because the readable data is device identifiers and non-confidential configuration; I:L because configuration changes alone have limited impact; A:N. Command injection and firmware replacement through the same interface are scored in their own records. If the management interface is IP-routed, use AV:N -> CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N = 5.3 MEDIUM.

timeline.value: DJI acknowledged the vulnerability and provided its assessment

solutions.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

supportingMedia.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

workarounds.value: Connect the unit's management Ethernet port only to an isolated network segment with no untrusted hosts, and do not route or bridge that segment to other networks, so that TCP port 16000 and the multicast discovery traffic (225.0.0.37, UDP port 16001) cannot be reached. cna.title: Pillow: Memory DoS in TIFF and EXIF IFD parsing via overlapping tag data

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 1.0 through 12.3.0, ImageFileDirectory_v2.load() in src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py retains a separate bytes object for each out-of-line IFD tag value without limiting the total data read or preventing distinct tags from referencing the same file region. A small crafted TIFF or EXIF-bearing JPEG, PNG, WebP, or MPO can therefore cause memory use quadratic in the input size. TIFF and some JPEG paths trigger parsing during Image.open(), while other formats are exposed when EXIF is requested, including through getexif() or ImageOps.exif_transpose(). The declared pixel dimensions do not bound this metadata allocation, so decompression-bomb checks do not prevent process memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

cna.title: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to Denial of Service via URL-encoded field size-limit bypass

descriptions.value: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart and url-encoded form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, the url-encoded parser stops accumulating a field only when the decoded length exactly equals the configured per-field size limit, and a malformed percent escape is passed through verbatim by the decoder, so the decoded length can jump from just below the limit to just above it and skip that equality check. The parser then keeps buffering the field in memory until the next delimiter or the end of the request, so a single unauthenticated url-encoded field or field name can grow to the size of the whole request body regardless of a much smaller configured per-field limit, with memory use bounded only by the independent whole-request body limit. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which clamps a field as soon as the decoded length reaches or exceeds the limit, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, set a conservative whole-request body limit so the per-field overshoot cannot exceed it.

descriptions.value: xschem 2.9.9 through 3.4.7 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in read_dataset() in src/rawtovcd.c due to an unchecked variable index. cna.title: gosaml2: Unauthenticated panic decrypting an EncryptedAssertion with a short or empty CipherValue

descriptions.value: gosaml2 is a Pure Go implementation of SAML 2.0. Prior to 0.12.0, ValidateEncodedResponse() calls decryptAssertions() on an EncryptedAssertion before signature or content validation completes, and EncryptedAssertion.DecryptBytes() in types/encrypted_assertion.go slices decoded ciphertext without first validating the required nonce or initialization-vector length. A CipherValue shorter than the 12-byte AES-GCM nonce causes a slice-bounds panic, and an empty AES-CBC CipherValue passes the modulo block-size check before causing a slice-bounds panic at the 16-byte initialization-vector split. An attacker needs only the service provider's public certificate to wrap a symmetric key, and no valid identity-provider signature or relationship is required. The unrecovered panic can terminate the request goroutine or the service process. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.0.

cna.title: OpenMage Magento-LTS before 20.18.2 Authorization Bypass via Forgeable RSS Order Key

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenMage Magento-LTS before 20.18.2 Authorization Bypass via Forgeable RSS Order Key

descriptions.value: OpenMage Magento-LTS before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an authorization bypass in the /rss/order/status feed because its URL key is unsigned Base64-encoded JSON of the order, increment, and customer ids. Unauthenticated attackers can forge keys from enumerated sequential ids to read other customers' names, items, prices, totals, and status comments when order-status RSS is enabled.

cna.title: Gitea required approval bypass through team review request removal

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #40268

descriptions.value: Removing a team's review request looked up a review by the negated team ID, which for the team with ID 2 is the ID of the built-in Actions user, and marked the review it found as official. In the organization that owns that team, a user who can change the review requests of a pull request could make an approval left by the Actions user count toward the approvals required by branch protection. Merging still required permission to merge. Removing a team review request no longer changes any review.

cna.title: NLTK: XMLCorpusView comment and CDATA parsing permits quadratic CPU denial of service

descriptions.value: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.

cna.title: All in One SEO <= 5.0.5 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'display_name' User Profile Field

affected.product: All in One SEO – AI SEO Plugin to Boost SEO Rankings & Traffic (Schema, Local SEO, Sitemap & SEO Insights)

descriptions.value: The All in One SEO – AI SEO Plugin to Boost SEO Rankings & Traffic (Schema, Local SEO, Sitemap & SEO Insights) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has placed the AIOSEO breadcrumb on the author template, that the site is running WordPress 6.6 or later with the core Interactivity runtime loaded (e.g., via a block theme or core/navigation block), and that a victim clicks the rendered breadcrumb link on the author archive page.

cna.title: SvelteKit: Build-time server-only module import guard could fail, resulting in server secrets being statically replaced in client bundle

descriptions.value: SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. cna.title: Dbus: server accept watch can be stalled by blocking nonce-tcp accept_with_noncefile path

workarounds.value:
Disable non-standard `nonce-tcp` listeners in the D-Bus configuration in favor of standard UNIX domain sockets. If network reachability is required, restrict access to trusted hosts using `firewalld`.

To remove an exposed port from an untrusted firewall zone:

```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-port=<PORT>/tcp
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<TRUSTED_IP_OR_SUBNET>
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Restricting or disabling network listeners prevents remote clients outside the trusted subnet from connecting to the affected bus.

Warning:
Reloading the firewall rules or altering the D-Bus server configuration requires restarting the affected D-Bus service, which will drop existing connections and temporarily disrupt communications.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in dbus when configured with the nonce-tcp transport. An unauthenticated attacker able to connect to an exposed listener can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by opening a connection and withholding the expected authentication token. Because the server processes this verification without enforcing a timeout, the stalled connection blocks the accept process and prevents legitimate clients from establishing new connections.

descriptions.description: Use of Blocking Code in Single-threaded, Non-blocking Context

cna.x_redhatCweChain: CWE-1322: Use of Blocking Code in Single-threaded, Non-blocking Context

cna.title: gittuf: Policy rules bypassed in the presence of global rules

solutions.value: Upgrade to gittuf 0.16.0 or later, which checks policy rules and global rules independently. Then re-run verification on the repository to make sure the vulnerability was not exploited.

descriptions.value: In gittuf 0.10.0 through 0.15.0, when a minimum threshold global rule and a policy rule protect the same namespace, verification gives the global rule's check over all trusted users in the policy precedence over the policy rule's own authorized users. A user listed in the policy file but not authorized by the policy rule, or fewer users than the rule's threshold, can make changes to the protected namespace that pass verification.

cna.title: NLTK: AllowlistUnpickler does not deny numpy submodule-local file-I/O sinks

descriptions.value: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, allowlisted_pickle_load keys dangerous NumPy globals by export name, allowing submodule-local numpy.lib file input/output callables to evade the denylist under the broad module allowance used by TransitionParser. When the development server is reachable from an untrusted network, Vite permits /_nuxt/@fs/ requests beneath that widened directory, allowing unauthenticated clients to read files such as credentials and SSH keys. cna.title: OpenTelemetry-Go: Eager W3C baggage-property materialization causes bounded memory-allocation amplification

descriptions.value: OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From version 1.0.0-RC1 until version 1.47.0, baggage.Parse and propagation.Baggage.Extract eagerly materialize every W3C baggage property through parseMember, grow property slices, serialize members, and copy properties into internal/baggage.Item. A valid densely populated baggage header can therefore cause allocation traffic and retained memory disproportionate to its bounded input size. Remote impact requires baggage extraction to be enabled, attacker-controlled input to reach it, and extraction to run before authentication or on a public route; the evidence establishes increased allocation and garbage-collection pressure but not reliable process termination. This issue is fixed in version 1.47.0.

cna.title: PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade

descriptions.value: CAPEC-475 Signature Spoofing by Improper Validation

PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: AIOHTTP: WebSocket max_msg_size bypass via integer overflow

Prior to 3.14.4, the C WebSocket reader adds a declared frame length to the size of an already buffered partial message using signed 64-bit arithmetic. A length near two to the power of 63 can overflow, allowing the max_msg_size check to pass. A remote peer can send a small non-final fragment followed by an oversized message and cause unbounded memory consumption. The Python WebSocket reader is unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

Prior to 3.14.4, Request.post() does not limit the number of fields in a URL-encoded form body, and inserting many repeated keys into MultiDict takes quadratic time on the event loop. A remote attacker can send a form POST within client_max_size to a handler that calls Request.post() and block the event loop. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: @grpc/grpc-js: RBAC override configs in VirtualHost and Route resources are not applied

descriptions.value: @grpc/grpc-js implements the core functionality of gRPC purely in JavaScript, without a C++ addon. From 1.14.0 through 1.14.1, XdsServer in @grpc/grpc-js-xds can acknowledge Route and VirtualHost resources while failing to apply their RBACPerRoute override configurations. The override parser is not registered under the override message type, override maps are stored under a type URL instead of the configured HTTP filter name, and VirtualHost override maps are not read. When experimental RBAC is enabled and a trusted xDS control plane supplies a broad top-level ALLOW policy with a stricter matching override, affected servers evaluate RPCs under the broad policy and can accept requests that should be denied. This issue is fixed in version 1.14.2.

cna.title: RabbitMQ MQTT Topic Permission Authorization Bypass

descriptions.value: RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. From 4.2.0 to before 4.2.4, RabbitMQ's MQTT plugin allows for topic-level authorization using regular expressions with variable substitution. Administrators can create patterns such as ^{client_id}-sensors$ to restrict user access to topics that include their client ID. However, the client_id is provided by the user in the MQTT CONNECT packet and is inserted into the regex pattern without escaping special regex characters. This flaw enables an authenticated MQTT user to inject regex operators to bypass authorization. This vulnerability is fixed in 4.2.4 and 4.3.0.

Prior to 7.0.7, 7.3.2, and 7.4, a CMS user with limited access to pages could copy a page they don't have access to to an area of the site they do. cna.title: Libunbound applications configured with 'unwanted-reply-threshold' could eventually be abruptly terminated

solutions.value: This issue is fixed starting with version 1.25.2

descriptions.value: With NLnet Labs Unbound up to and including version 1.25.1, applications using libunbound and configured with 'unwanted-reply-threshold', could eventually be abruptly terminated if the threshold is reached and libunbound needs to call 'libworker_alloc_cleanup' since the function is absent from the function call allow list. When an application using libunbound sets 'unwanted-reply-threshold' to any non-zero value and the iterator queries an authoritative that replies with enough wrong-transaction-ID UDP datagrams to cross the threshold, the 'libworker_alloc_cleanup' will eventually be called. Since the function is absent from the function call allow list, this leads to a fatal exit of libunbound and eventual termination of the embedding application.Unbound itself is not affected since its relevant function 'worker_alloc_cleanup' is registed in the allow list and proceeds to perform the documented cache flush.

cna.title: gittuf: Policy can be rolled back to prior valid version

descriptions.value: gittuf is a platform-agnostic Git security system. Prior to 0.14.0, an attacker with push access to gittuf's Reference State Log (RSL) can roll back the current policy to any previous policy trusted by the current set of root keys. gittuf determines the policy to load by inspecting the RSL. Except for the very first policy (which is automatically trusted given gittuf's TOFU model, or verified against manually specified keys), whenever an RSL entry that points to a new policy is encountered, gittuf validates that this policy is trusted. This is done by checking that the new policy’s root metadata is signed by the required threshold of the current policy's root keys. Because of this, an attacker with push access to the RSL may create a new entry that references an old policy (that is trusted by the most recent policy's set of root keys), thereby rolling back gittuf's policy to the attacker's chosen state.  This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.0.

cna.title: protobufjs-cli: Code injection in pbjs static output from crafted schema names

descriptions.value: protobufjs-cli is the command line add-on for protobuf.js. Prior to 1.2.1 and 2.0.2, pbjs static code generation could emit unsafe JavaScript identifiers derived from schema-controlled names. When generating static JavaScript from a crafted schema or JSON descriptor, certain namespace, enum, service, or derived full names could be written into the generated output without sufficient sanitization. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.2.1 and 2.0.2.

cna.title: Portainer: Kubernetes middleware continues after token validation failure, bypassing endpoint authorization

descriptions.value: Portainer Community Edition is a lightweight service delivery platform for containerized applications that can be used to manage Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes and ACI environments. From 2.33.0 to before 2.33., Portainer proxies requests to Kubernetes clusters through a middleware layer (kubeClientMiddleware) that validates the requesting user's token before forwarding traffic to the cluster. When security.RetrieveTokenData returned an error, the middleware wrote an HTTP 403 response but was missing a return statement — execution continued into the handler with a nil tokenData value. The Kubernetes endpoints sit behind Portainer's outer AuthenticatedAccess bouncer, so an attacker requires a valid Portainer session. However, a user whose secondary token validation fails in kubeClientMiddleware — for example a user without permission to access a given Kubernetes endpoint — would have their request forwarded to the cluster anyway, bypassing the authorization check. The same defect was present in both the CE and EE codebases. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.33.8.

cna.title: Snappier: Infinite loop in SnappyStream decompression on malformed framed input

descriptions.value: Snappier is a high performance C# implementation of the Snappy compression algorithm. Prior to 1.3.1, Snappier.SnappyStream enters an uncatchable infinite loop when decompressing a malformed framed-format Snappy stream as small as 15 bytes. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.3.1.

cna.title: Vanetza: Remote Denial of Service via Uncaught OER Encoding Exception in Cryptographic Verification

descriptions.value: Vanetza is an open-source implementation of the ETSI C-ITS protocol suite. In 26.02 and earlier, a denial-of-service vulnerability was identified in the cryptographic verification pipeline of Vanetza. When processing incoming V2X messages, the ASN.1 decoder accepts the structure as syntactically valid. However, this reveals a logic-based protocol failure where semantic constraints on specific fields are only strictly enforced during OER re-encoding. Specifically, if a crafted packet contains a certificate where the Psid (Provider Service Identifier) sub-type violates subtype constraints (e.g., out-of-range or invalid CHOICE variant), it is accepted during initial parsing, where subtype constraints are not enforced. Later, when StraightVerifyService attempts to calculate a message hash for cryptographic verification, it must re-encode the signing certificate. The underlying ASN.1 wrapper (asn1c_wrapper.cpp) detects the semantic violation during encoding and raises a std::runtime_error. This exception is not caught within the encoding path and propagates to std::terminate, resulting in immediate process termination. This vulnerability is fixed with commit e1a2e2709210d309458c3d77f98d50dec26c0df0.

cna.title: Spring Cloud AWS: Missing SNS message signature verification allows spoofing of HTTP/HTTPS endpoint notifications

descriptions.value: Spring Cloud AWS simplifies using AWS managed services in a Spring and Spring Boot applications. From 3.0.0 to 4.0.1, pplications using Spring Cloud AWS SNS HTTP/HTTPS endpoint support (@NotificationMessageMapping, @NotificationSubscriptionMapping, @NotificationUnsubscribeConfirmationMapping) did not verify the signature of incoming SNS messages. An unauthenticated attacker who knows the endpoint URL could send crafted HTTP POST requests mimicking SNS Notification or SubscriptionConfirmation messages. This vulnerability is fixed in 4.0.2.

cna.title: efw4.X: RCE via zipslip

descriptions.value: efw4.X is an Enterprise Framework for Web. Prior to 4.08.010, efw.file.FileManager.unZip writes zip entries to disk using new File(baseDir, zipEntry.getName()) with no canonical-path check. An entry name such as ../../../pwned.jsp escapes the intended extraction directory and lands anywhere the Tomcat process can write — including the servlet context root. Combined with the framework's multipart /uploadServlet and an event that calls file.saveUploadFiles + FileManager.unZip, a remote attacker with no credentials drops a JSP webshell and executes arbitrary commands as the Tomcat user. This vulnerability is fixed in 4.08.010.

cna.title: free5GC: SMF UPI DELETE /upi/v1/upNodesLinks/{ref} panics on AN-node deletion via nil UPF dereference; unauthenticated, state-mutating

descriptions.value: free5GC is an open-source implementation of the 5G core network. Prior to 4.2.2, free5GC's SMF mounts the UPI management route group without inbound OAuth2 middleware. On top of that, the DELETE /upi/v1/upNodesLinks/{upNodeRef} handler unconditionally dereferences upNode.UPF after the type-guarded async release, even though AN-typed nodes are constructed without a UPF object. As a result, a single unauthenticated DELETE /upi/v1/upNodesLinks/gNB1 request crashes the handler with a nil-pointer panic AND mutates the in-memory user-plane topology before panicking (the UpNodeDelete(upNodeRef) line runs first). This is an unauthenticated, state-mutating panic-DoS sink that an off-path network attacker can trigger by name against any AN entry. This vulnerability is fixed in 4.2.2.
